title: feat(wallet): fail-closed onlineTopUpLimit submit and versioned admin CAS (T-04.2.02.06)
body:
## What
- Submission now **fails closed** when a persisted `finance.wallet_top_up_limit` row cannot be read as a valid integer IRR ceiling. A corrupt value no longer substitutes the 2,000,000,000 IRR default, so it cannot silently raise the enforced cap. Wallet GET omits `onlineTopUpLimit` in that case so the customer form already fail-closes client-side.
- Missing rows still serve the default 2e9 IRR at config version `0`. Valid persisted limits continue to be re-read under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` + `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` before the Pending INSERT, and over-limit 400s still return the enforced `{ onlineTopUpLimit, configVersion }` snapshot for retry with a reduced amount.
- Admin PUT `/api/admin/config/wallet-top-up-limit` accepts optional `expected_version`. When present it is compared to the locked `app_config.version` (or `0` when the row is absent) and a mismatch returns 409 `CONFLICT:VERSION_CONFLICT` without writing. The admin panel always sends the loaded version, reloads on 409, and shows a bilingual conflict message.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Admin-configurable `onlineTopUpLimit` with default 2,000,000,000 IRR — GET/PUT `/api/admin/config/wallet-top-up-limit`; missing rows serve the default at version `0`.
- [x] Versioned config — `app_config.version` increments on write, global `config_version` is bumped, cache is invalidated, and a provided `expected_version` is compare-and-swapped against the locked row so a stale admin editor cannot clobber a later write.
- [x] Enforced at submission — `OnlineTopUpService.initiate` re-reads the locked config before INSERT; amounts above the current ceiling are rejected with 400 and no ledger row. A corrupt persisted row now fails closed (400, no snapshot, no Pending row) instead of applying the 2e9 default.
- [x] Absent-row/first-write race is serialized — submission and admin update share `pg_advisory_xact_lock`. Covered by the existing real-PostgreSQL concurrency test.
- [x] Retry with reduced amount — a later, lower limit applies to new submissions; in-flight Pending rows can be replayed with the original idempotency key. Over-limit 400s still carry the enforced snapshot.
- [x] Admin UI warning that changing the limit affects future online top-ups only; panel is RTL-aware and now sends `expected_version`.
- [x] Bank-receipt top-ups remain uncapped (unchanged).

## Validation
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (44 files, 620 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass

title: feat(wallet): include overpayment split on bank-receipt completed notice (T-04.2.02.05)

- Invoice-linked bank-receipt confirmation already settles `min(receipt, remaining)` on the invoice and credits only the excess via a separate `WalletService.credit()` with `bankReceiptOverpaymentCreditIdempotencyKey` (never over-settles `paid_amount`).

title: feat(invoice): dual-approval check for high-value bank receipt confirmation (T-04.3.01.05)
body:
## What
- Gate staff confirmation of invoice bank receipts on the admin-configured `finance.dual_approval_threshold`.
- When the receipt amount is **≥** the enabled threshold, the first finance staff confirm parks the receipt in `UnderReview` and records a pending `bank_payment_confirmation` approval request. Invoice `paid_amount` and the wallet are unchanged until a **second, different** finance staff member confirms.
- Same-staff retry of a parked confirm is idempotent. Rejecting a parked receipt now **locks** the pending approval request and resolves it through `applyApprovalRequestResolutionOnClient` (decision `reject`) so the different-reviewer check and canonical `approval_request_rejected` audit row commit in the same transaction as the receipt reject. The initiator cannot reject their own pending request (403); a second finance staff member must reject.
- A DualApprovalService rejection of that pending request is **terminal**: a later confirm does not mint a replacement pending request. The receipt is synchronized to `Rejected` (review reason copied onto `rejection_reason`) and confirmation returns 409.
- Second-staff confirmation resolves the pending request through `applyApprovalRequestResolutionOnClient` (decision `approve`) so different-user review and the canonical `approval_request_approved` audit row commit in the same transaction as settlement.
- Missing or `0` threshold disables the gate (existing single-staff confirm). A corrupt stored threshold fails closed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Receipt amount **below** the admin-configured threshold still confirms in one finance staff step (verified in unit + integration tests).
- [x] Receipt amount **equal to** the threshold requires a second, different finance staff confirmation before settlement (T-04.3.01.05 uses ≥; verified).
- [x] Receipt amount **above** the threshold is parked the same way (verified).
- [x] First confirmer cannot complete the parked confirm; a second finance staff member settles and is recorded as `confirmed_by` (verified).
- [x] Dual approval disabled (`0` or missing `app_config` row) leaves the existing single-confirm path unchanged (verified).
- [x] Corrupt stored threshold blocks confirmation without settling (fail closed; verified).
- [x] Reject of a parked receipt stores the reason, notifies the customer, resolves the pending approval request through the canonical dual-approval path, writes `approval_request_rejected`, and does not credit the wallet (verified).
- [x] The initiator cannot reject their own pending dual-approval request via the receipt reject API (403; verified in unit + integration tests).
- [x] DualApprovalService rejection of the pending request cannot be discarded by retrying confirm; the receipt is synchronized to Rejected and no replacement request is created (verified in unit + integration tests).
- [x] Second-staff confirmation writes the canonical `approval_request_approved` audit row atomically with settlement (verified in unit + integration tests).

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared exec vitest run src/finance/invoice-bank-receipt-dual-approval.test.ts src/finance/invoice-bank-receipt-confirmation.test.ts` — pass (21 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/admin/dual-approval-resolution.test.ts src/admin/dual-approval.service.test.ts src/invoice/invoice-bank-receipt-confirmation.service.test.ts src/admin/invoice-bank-receipt-confirmation.controller.test.ts src/admin/dual-approval.controller.test.ts` — pass (64 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/invoice/invoice-bank-receipt-confirmation.integration.test.ts src/invoice/invoice-bank-receipt-rejection.integration.test.ts src/invoice/invoice-bank-receipt-dual-approval.integration.test.ts` — pass (22 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db test` — not run (no schema/migration change in this task)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web test` — not available / not applicable (no UI in this task)

## Risks / limitations
- Completing dual approval is done through the existing staff confirm endpoint (second staff POSTs confirm). Approving the matching row in the generic dual-approval queue marks the request approved but does not by itself settle the receipt; a subsequent confirm still performs settlement.
- DualApprovalService rejection does not itself mutate `bank_receipts`; the next confirm call synchronizes the receipt to `Rejected`. Until that confirm (or a receipt-reject API call by a different staff member), the receipt can still appear as `UnderReview`.
- The generic T-09.07.02 `shouldRequireDualApproval` helper still uses a strict `>` comparison; this bank-receipt gate uses **≥** as specified by T-04.3.01.05 / C-04.CC.02.
- Initiator cancellation of a parked receipt is not modeled as a separate audited cancellation: the first confirmer must wait for a different finance staff member to reject (same dual-control as confirm).

title: feat(invoice): customer bank-receipt upload with amount and file validation (T-04.3.01.02)
body:
## What
- Customer invoice bank-receipt upload: `POST /api/invoices/:invoiceId/bank-receipts` validates a positive int8 IRR amount, PDF/JPEG/PNG/WebP type, and category size caps (document 10 MB, image 20 MB), then inserts a profile-scoped `bank_receipts` row in `Submitted`.
- Submit no longer trusts the recorded `storage_records` MIME or a mutable upload key. It re-reads the object, magic-byte sniffs the bytes, copies that buffer to a server-only `receipts/submitted/<uuid>.<ext>` key (presigned PUT URLs are issued only under `uploads/<category>/`), and stores the sealed key on the receipt.
- File-size enforcement uses the actual copied byte count, capped at the category limit. A forged small recorded `file_size` with a large object is rejected. ZIP (or other disallowed) bytes are rejected even when the recorded content type is still PDF.
- After submit, overwriting the original presigned PUT object cannot change the sealed copy or the stored receipt. Matching retries of the same customer upload key return the original row without recopying.
- Amount input maps Persian/Arabic-Indic digits and strips only well-formed thousands grouping (`,` / `٬`). Decimals, signs, exponent notation, and alphabetic pasted text are preserved so submit validation fails instead of concatenating leftover digit groups into a different IRR amount.
- The stored object must be a verified `bank_receipt` owned by the caller; both the original upload record and the sealed copy are frozen `immutable` in the same transaction.
- Wallet top-up and invoice upload share one advisory-lock namespace and a `bank_receipt_attachment_claims` row (`storage_key` unique, `claim_type` wallet_topup | invoice_receipt). A claim owned by the other flow is rejected; same-flow retries still reuse the original row.
- Invoice details shows an RTL-aware upload form for Unpaid / PaymentUnderReview / PartiallyFunded (non-credit) invoices. Invoice settlement and wallet credit are left to later tasks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Amount must be a positive integer IRR value — shared parser, API, and UI reject 0 / negative before insert (unit + integration). Client normalization no longer turns `12.5`, `1e3`, `-100`, or `abc12` into a different positive integer.
- [x] File type is limited to PDF or JPEG/PNG/WebP — attachment-key extensions plus magic-byte sniff at submit; ZIP/exe/video rejected even when recorded MIME still says PDF.
- [x] File size is capped at 10 MB (document) / 20 MB (image) — client guard plus actual object bytes at submit; forged small `fileSize` with a large object is rejected (unit + PostgreSQL integration).
- [x] A valid upload creates a `bank_receipts` row in `Submitted` bound to the sealed copy key; invoice state is unchanged.
- [x] Profile isolation: other-profile invoices 404; Paid / credit-note invoices 409; unique attachment identity is the customer upload key (claim) plus sealed copy key (receipt row). Matching retries return the original row.
- [x] Cross-flow uniqueness: the same storage key cannot be claimed as both a wallet top-up and an invoice receipt (sequential and concurrent PostgreSQL tests).
- [x] Authoritative type validation cannot be bypassed by replacing the original object through a still-valid presigned PUT URL before or after submit (sniff + sealed copy; overwrite-after-submit integration test).
- [x] Web production build no longer imports `node:crypto` from the shared finance barrel (`pnpm build` / Vite).

title: feat(invoice): add bank_receipts table for staff confirmation (T-04.3.01.01)
body:
## What
- Add the `bank_receipts` table (migration 0078) as the durable invoice bank-receipt evidence row for S-04.3.01: `id`, `invoiceId`, `profileId`, `amount`, `paymentDate`, `payerReference`, `attachmentKey`, `customerNote`, `state`, optional `confirmedBy` / `confirmedAt` / `rejectionReason`, and timestamps.
- Enforce the S-04.3.01 lifecycle at the database: `Submitted` (default) → `UnderReview` → `Confirmed` | `Rejected`, with positive IRR amounts, unique `attachment_key`, paired confirmation/rejection columns, and RESTRICT FKs to profiles and users.
- Bind each receipt to the invoice it pays with a composite foreign key `(invoice_id, profile_id) REFERENCES invoices(id, profile_id)` (backed by `uq_invoices_id_profile_id`), so a receipt cannot be stored against another profile's invoice.
- Fail closed when `invoices`, `profiles`, or `users` are missing so Drizzle cannot record 0078 as applied without creating the table and foreign keys. Isolated migrator tests seed those prerequisites before `migrate()`.
- Fix greenfield helpers: `createBankReceiptsTable` now adds guarded `uq_invoices_id_profile_id UNIQUE (id, profile_id)` before `CREATE TABLE`, and `createInvoicesTable` declares the same constraint so `createInvoicesTable` then `createBankReceiptsTable` succeeds against PostgreSQL.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `bank_receipts` exists with `id`, `invoiceId`, `profileId`, `amount`, `paymentDate`, `payerReference`, `attachmentKey`, `customerNote`, `state`, optional `confirmedBy` / `confirmedAt` / `rejectionReason`, and `created_at` / `updated_at`.
- [x] `state` is constrained to `Submitted | UnderReview | Confirmed | Rejected` (default `Submitted`).
- [x] `amount` is a positive int8 IRR value (`CHECK amount > 0`).
- [x] `paymentDate` is a calendar `DATE`; confirmation columns are set together only on `Confirmed`; `rejectionReason` is required only on `Rejected`.
- [x] A receipt whose `profile_id` does not own the referenced invoice is rejected by `fk_bank_receipts_invoice_profile` (PostgreSQL 23503).

title: feat(wallet): bind chargeback event ids to the claimed notification payload (T-04.2.04.02)
body:
## What
- HMAC-authenticated `POST /api/wallet/top-ups/chargeback` parses inbound provider chargeback/reversal notifications, validates the same signed-content scheme as online top-up callbacks, and maps a unique Completed top-up credit (merchant order id, then provider ref, then authority) before calling `WalletService.reverseTransaction`.
- Event-id idempotency is bound to the claimed notification for every stored row, including terminal `reversed`, `unmatched`, and `unresolved` events. A retry resumes or returns the stored outcome only when the canonical payload digest matches the persisted `raw` snapshot. A validly signed retry that reuses the event id with a different locator, amount, or merchant payload is rejected and never remapped, reversed, or used to build a finance alert.
- Chargeback handlers reverse on the same pooled connection that holds the session advisory lock, so `reverseTransaction` cannot wait on a nested checkout. Concurrent notifications therefore cannot fill the pool with lock connections and deadlock. A regression test runs four handlers against a pool whose max is 4 and asserts completion within 8s.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests prove a matching `processing` resume still reverses once; mutated retries cannot reverse `processing`, `reversed`, `unmatched`, or `unresolved` events; a corrected locator after an unmatched event is rejected without remapping; concurrent retries of the same event id serialize to one reversal; two concurrent event ids for the same top-up share one compensating ledger row; and bounded-pool concurrency completes without deadlock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Parse inbound notification — verified: `parseChargebackNotificationJson` accepts `chargeback` / `reversed` / `reversal`, merchant id, positive IRR amount, and locators; omitted locators parse as null; rejects invalid JSON, types, amounts, and non-UUID order ids (`packages/shared` tests).
- [x] Validate signature — verified: missing secret → 503; missing HMAC headers → 401; tampered HMAC → 401 before any mapping/reversal; replay window → 401; merchant mismatch → 401. Integration test proves a wrong secret never writes `wallet_chargeback_events`.
- [x] Map to original top-up — verified: unique Completed credit matched by pending order id first, then provider ref, then authority; locator-less / amount mismatch / ambiguity / wrong type or state → unmatched. `hasChargebackLocator` fails closed before matching.
- [x] Compensating transaction, not history rewrite — verified: original top-up row stays Completed; reversal posts the opposite amount via `reverseTransaction`. Concurrent same-event and distinct-event races post exactly one reversal.
- [x] Untraceable chargeback is a general exception — verified: unmatched event stored with null original/wallet FKs and no extra ledger rows.
- [x] Event-id retries stay bound to one immutable notification — verified: stored `raw` is compared before branching on status; unit tests reject changed locators against `processing`, `reversed`, `unmatched`, and `unresolved`; integration tests prove a mutated processing retry, a corrected locator after unmatched, and payload mismatch against `reversed`/`unresolved` never reverse another top-up.
- [x] Nested pool checkout cannot deadlock chargeback handlers — verified: `reverseTransaction` runs on the advisory-lock client inside that session's transaction; integration pool max equals concurrent handler count (4) and the bounded-pool test completes within 8s.
- [ ] Finance alert (push + dashboard) — not this task; owned by T-04.2.04.03 (already on main). Unmatched/unresolved events remain the input to that alert path. Duplicate unmatched retries with an identical payload still re-attempt the alert; mismatched payloads are rejected first so alert data cannot be built from a different notification.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (40 files / 571 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db test` — pass (66 files / 500 tests)
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/wallet/chargeback-detection src/wallet/payment-gateway.test.ts` (in `apps/api`) — pass (4 files / 85 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm lint` — not available (turbo reports no lint tasks in this repo)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web test` — not applicable (no web UI in this task)

## Risks / limitations
- Provider chargeback HMAC uses the existing payment-callback signed-content format (`eventId.timestamp.rawBody`); adapters that speak a different signature scheme will need a later adapter.
- Finance alerting and dashboard warnings remain T-04.2.04.03; this task only detects, maps, reverses, and persists unmatched/unresolved events.
- A mismatched retry is rejected without rewriting the stored event, so a later retry with the original payload can still complete or replay it. A corrected locator must use a new event id.

title: test(wallet): concurrent payInvoiceWithWallet in-flight and reserve races (T-04.2.03.04)
body:
## What
- Extend the real-PostgreSQL `payInvoiceWithWallet` concurrency suite (T-04.2.03.04) against the current FOR UPDATE + fail-closed `(idempotencyKey, entityType)` implementation.
- Concurrent retries against a live in-flight (NULL response) claim all 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` and never debit, settle, or write audit.
- Concurrent retries of an expired in-flight claim reclaim exactly once: one Paid original, two replays, one ledger row.
- Three invoices racing for funds that cover two remainings: two settle Paid, one fails insufficient with `available=0`, two ledger rows, postedBalance 0.
- A wallet reserve racing a remaining debit of the last available rial: exactly one succeeds, one ledger row, no deadlock.

Existing coverage kept: three distinct-key payments of one invoice (one Paid, two already-paid), concurrent same-key retries (one original, two replays), sequential duplicate-key replay, same-key collision across invoices, sequential and concurrent insufficient balance (including reserved funds), two-invoice overdraw and both-funded races, PartiallyFunded remaining race, and credit-vs-pay lock-order safety.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Concurrent payment attempts (one succeeds, others fail) — three distinct-key payments of one invoice: 1 fulfilled Paid, 2 `ConflictException` already-paid, one `wallet_transactions` row, postedBalance reduced once; losing keys leave no `idempotency_keys` rows. Two of three invoices succeed when funds cover two remainings.
- [x] Duplicate idempotency key — three concurrent same-key retries all fulfill (one `replayed: false`, two `replayed: true`); sequential retry returns `replayed: true`; concurrent reuse on a different invoice 409s (`IDEMPOTENCY_COLLISION`). Live in-flight same-key retries all 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` without debiting. Expired in-flight reclaim: exactly one original debit, two replays.
- [x] Insufficient balance — sequential, concurrent, and reserved-funds cases roll wallet, invoice, ledger, and audit back; the two-of-three funds race leaves the loser Unpaid with `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE(0, remaining)`.
- [x] Race conditions — two invoices / funds for one remaining: one Paid; funds for both: both Paid; PartiallyFunded remaining: one Paid; credit-vs-pay: no deadlock; reserve-vs-pay of the last rial: exactly one succeeds.

title: feat(wallet): FOR UPDATE transaction for pay-from-wallet settlement (T-04.2.03.02)
body:
## What
- Keep wallet debit, invoice → Paid, `wallet_transactions` insert, and wallet/invoice audit in one DB transaction that `SELECT … FOR UPDATE OF wallets` then `… OF invoices` (stable lock order).
- Gate the debit on the locked `availableBalance` (`posted − reserved`) snapshot; pass that snapshot’s `version` into `WalletService.debit` as `expectedVersion` so a stale lock cannot complete.
- Update `paid_amount` only when the locked invoice `state` still matches, then transition Unpaid / PartiallyFunded → Paid on the same client.
- Integration test now requires `RowShareLock` on both rows and proves a second session’s `SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` fails with `55P03` before debit.

- [x] One DB transaction locks the wallet row then the invoice row with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` — verified by unit lock-order assertions (`FOR UPDATE OF wallets` before `FOR UPDATE OF invoices`) and PostgreSQL `RowShareLock` + `NOWAIT` (`55P03`) integration coverage.
- [x] Available balance is validated from the locked snapshot (`posted − reserved`); insufficient or reserved-consumed balance rolls back with no ledger, Paid, or audit writes.
- [x] Wallet debit of the exact remaining amount runs on the same client, bound to the locked `version`; invoice is updated to Paid with `wallet_transactions` + `wallet.invoice_payment` / `invoice.pay_from_wallet` audit in the same commit.

title: feat(wallet): settle invoices only after an exact remaining debit (T-04.2.03.01)
body:
## What
- `PayInvoiceWithWalletService.payInvoiceWithWallet(invoiceId, profileId, idempotencyKey)` already settles an Unpaid or PartiallyFunded invoice with a **single full wallet debit** of the exact remaining IRR amount in one DB transaction (wallet `FOR UPDATE`, then invoice, then `WalletService.debit` on the caller client, then Paid).
- This change **fail-closes before Paid** unless the posted ledger row is a Completed `payment` debit of **exactly `-remaining`** for this invoice and wallet (`isExactRemainingWalletDebit`).
- Colliding `WalletService.debit` idempotency keys (`Idempotency key already used…`) are mapped to `PAY_INVOICE_WITH_WALLET_ERRORS.IDEMPOTENCY_COLLISION()` and roll back, so a partial or unrelated debit cannot mark the invoice Paid.

- [x] Invoice becomes `Paid` and wallet posted balance is reduced via `WalletService.debit` (unit-tested; real-DB concurrency coverage is T-04.2.03.04).

title: fix(wallet): keep online top-up TTL expiry single-writer under concurrency (T-04.2.02.07)
body:
## What
- The worker expiry cron (`online_topup_expiry_scan`) already auto-rejects online `topup` ledger rows that stay `Pending` past the TTL without crediting the wallet (merged in #270 / #281). This PR finishes T-04.2.02.07 against current `main` by making the reject compare-and-set match the candidate predicate.
- `REJECT_EXPIRED_ONLINE_TOPUP_SQL` now requires `metadata.channel = 'online'` in addition to `type = topup` and `state = Pending`, so a locked non-online row cannot be stamped `Rejected`.
- Real-PostgreSQL coverage proves: `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` skips a held intent and leaves it `Pending`; two overlapping scanners credit exactly one `wallet.online_topup.expired` audit; a truncated tick drains the remainder oldest-first; env `ONLINE_TOPUP_PENDING_TTL_MS` is used when `ttlMs` is omitted.
- Provider authority on `metadata.gateway` is still preserved via JSONB merge so a later authenticated callback can credit a TTL-expired `Rejected` intent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Online `topup` rows still `Pending` after the TTL are auto-rejected to `Rejected` without changing wallet balances — covered by existing scanner unit + PostgreSQL tests (re-run in this PR).
- [x] Bank-receipt Pendings are excluded (`metadata.channel = 'online'` only) — candidate SQL, eligibility re-check, and now the reject UPDATE.
- [x] Expiry is safe under concurrency: SKIP LOCKED skips a held row; overlapping scanners reject once and write one audit.
- [x] Bounded drain continues on the next tick (truncated batch, oldest-created first).
- [x] Provider reference stays reconcilable after expiry — JSONB merge keeps `metadata.gateway`; callback tests on `main` credit TTL-expired `Rejected` rows (not changed in this PR).

title: feat(wallet): return enforced onlineTopUpLimit on over-limit submit (T-04.2.02.06)
body:
## What
- Versioned admin `onlineTopUpLimit` (default 2,000,000,000 IRR) is already persisted in `app_config` (`finance.wallet_top_up_limit`), bumped on write, cache-invalidated, and re-enforced under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` at online top-up INSERT (landed in #269 / #280).
- Over-limit submit now returns the **enforced** `{ onlineTopUpLimit, configVersion }` on the 400 body. The global HTTP exception filter forwards only that validated snapshot onto `error`, so a stale wallet GET cannot hide the ceiling that actually rejected the amount.
- The customer form reads that production error shape (`error.message` plus the snapshot), refreshes the advertised cap, rotates the idempotency key, and keeps “retry with a reduced amount” as the recovery path.

title: fix(wallet): credit bank-receipt excess only on payable or paid invoices (T-04.2.02.05)
body:
## What
- Invoice-linked bank-receipt confirmation already splits a receipt at remaining (`min(receipt, remaining)` onto the invoice; any excess is a **separate** verified wallet credit via `WalletService.credit()` with `wallet-bank-receipt-overpayment-credit:<pendingId>`). This follow-up keeps that split and closes two gaps after the staff-review UI landed.
- Staff can bind a receipt only to **Unpaid / PaymentUnderReview / PartiallyFunded / Paid**. Payable states settle up to remaining and credit excess. **Paid** has remaining 0, so the whole receipt is wallet excess and the invoice is untouched. **Draft / Overdue / Cancelled / Refunded / PartiallyRefunded** return 409 instead of silently crediting the wallet.
- Staff confirm now waits for a successful allocation preview before posting, and the step-up retry uses the **invoice id captured at first click** so the posted split matches the preview.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] If receipt amount > invoice remaining, excess is credited to the wallet as a distinct ledger row (not invoice over-settlement). Verified by existing unit and PostgreSQL integration tests; Paid invoices with remaining 0 credit the full receipt to the wallet.

- [x] Overpayment credit uses a separate idempotency key from the wallet-top-up credit. Confirm retries do not bump `paid_amount` or posted balance again.
- [x] Closed invoices cannot be used as an overpayment target: Cancelled (and Draft / Overdue / Refunded / PartiallyRefunded) return 409, leave paid amount/state unchanged, and do not credit the wallet. Verified in unit and PostgreSQL integration tests.
- [x] Staff UI (RTL/FA+EN) previews remaining vs excess, blocks confirm until that preview succeeds, and reuses the captured invoice id after step-up. Verified by component tests.

title: feat(wallet): keep reverseTransaction the only compensating reversal writer (T-04.2.04.01)
body:
## What
- `WalletService.reverseTransaction(originalTransactionId, reason, idempotencyKey)` remains the compensating reversal writer: it inserts a Completed `reversal` row with the opposite signed amount, links `reverses_transaction_id`, and adjusts `posted_balance` without rewriting the original.
- `credit()` / `debit()` refuse `type: 'reversal'` so an unlinked reversal cannot bypass that unique original pointer.
- Migration `0077_wallet_tx_reversal_original_check` adds CHECK `chk_wallet_tx_reversal_original` as **NOT VALID** so legacy `type = 'reversal'` rows without `reverses_transaction_id` (legal under 0074 / credit-debit) cannot fail deploy. New writes are still enforced.
- The same migration copies violating rows into `wallet_tx_reversal_check_violations` (idempotent `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) and documents the audited staff reconciliation procedure. VALIDATE is deferred to a later contract-phase migration after operators reconcile those rows. Ledger history is not rewritten automatically.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `reverseTransaction(originalTransactionId, reason, idempotencyKey)` creates a compensating reversal transaction and adjusts posted balance — verified by unit and real-PostgreSQL integration tests (credit reversal, debit reversal, idempotent retry, unique original, concurrent races, insufficient available balance, caller-owned transaction rollback).
- [x] Original ledger rows are not rewritten; corrections are append-only compensating entries — verified by integration tests that the original stays `Completed` with its original amount.
- [x] One original can be reversed at most once (`uq_wallet_tx_reverses_transaction`) and every **new** `reversal` row must point at that original (`chk_wallet_tx_reversal_original`, NOT VALID) — verified by schema/migrate PostgreSQL tests, including an upgrade-path test that a 0074 unlinked reversal survives 0077, is reported in `wallet_tx_reversal_check_violations`, and new unlinked reversals still fail with 23514.

title: test(wallet): concurrent payInvoiceWithWallet races (T-04.2.03.04)
body:
## What
- Extend the real-PostgreSQL `payInvoiceWithWallet` concurrency suite (T-04.2.03.04) against the completed FOR UPDATE + unique `(idempotencyKey, entityType)` implementation.
- Concurrent distinct-key payments of one invoice: exactly one Paid debit; losers fail already-paid and roll back their `idempotency_keys` claims.
- Concurrent same-key retries all fulfill (one original, two replays, one ledger row). Sequential duplicate keys replay; the same key racing on two invoices is a collision and leaves the loser Unpaid.
- Insufficient availableBalance — sequential, concurrent, and reserved-funds cases — rolls wallet, invoice, ledger, and audit back.
- Two invoices racing for funds that cover only one remaining: one Paid. When funds cover both, both Paid. Concurrent remaining debits of a PartiallyFunded invoice settle once. A wallet credit racing a pay-from-wallet debit completes without deadlock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Concurrent payment attempts (one succeeds, others fail) — three distinct-key payments of one invoice: 1 fulfilled Paid, 2 `ConflictException` already-paid, one `wallet_transactions` row, postedBalance reduced once; losing keys leave no `idempotency_keys` rows.
- [x] Duplicate idempotency key — three concurrent same-key retries all fulfill (no `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`); exactly one `replayed: false` and two `replayed: true`; sequential retry returns `replayed: true`; concurrent reuse of the same key on a different invoice 409s (`IDEMPOTENCY_COLLISION`) and leaves that invoice Unpaid.
- [x] Insufficient balance — sequential and concurrent short-balance attempts throw `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, including when reserved funds leave available below remaining; wallet/invoice/ledger/audit unchanged.
- [x] Race conditions — two invoices on one wallet with funds for only one remaining: exactly one Paid; with funds for both remainings: both Paid; PartiallyFunded remaining races settle once; pay-from-wallet vs wallet credit on the same row completes without deadlock.

## What

This follow-up keeps that server path and closes remaining client fail-closed gaps.
- Customer wallet GET still advertises `{ onlineTopUpLimit, configVersion }`. The top-up form now treats a missing or invalid advertised ceiling as fail-closed: it does not POST, and the submit control stays disabled. A configured `0` kill switch is also disabled client-side.
- Server 400 on a later tighter ceiling (stale GET vs locked submit) is still mapped to the limit-exceeded message so a retry with a reduced amount remains the recovery path.
- Admin GET `/api/admin/config/wallet-top-up-limit` now sends credentials like PUT. Staff who lack `admin:financial:edit` (403) no longer see a load-error panel on the wallet receipts page.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Admin-configurable `onlineTopUpLimit` with default 2,000,000,000 IRR — GET/PUT `/api/admin/config/wallet-top-up-limit`; missing rows serve the default at version `0`. Covered by existing API unit tests; not changed in this follow-up.
- [x] Versioned config — `app_config.version` increments on write, global `config_version` is bumped, and `ConfigCache.invalidate` runs after commit. Covered by existing admin service tests; not changed in this follow-up.
- [x] Enforced at submission — `OnlineTopUpService.initiate` re-reads the locked config before INSERT; amounts above the current ceiling are rejected with 400 and no ledger row. Covered by existing API unit/integration tests; not changed in this follow-up.

title: feat(wallet): finance alert for unresolved chargebacks (T-04.2.04.03)
body:
## What
- Enqueue an immediate `finance.chargeback_unresolved` outbox notification (in-app push + email) to Finance-role staff and platform admins when a provider chargeback stays `unmatched` or the compensating reversal cannot post (`unresolved`).
- Replays of the same event id are idempotent (`finance.chargeback_unresolved:<eventId>:<profileId>`), so a retried webhook cannot duplicate the alert.
- Expose `GET /api/admin/wallet/chargebacks/unresolved-warning` and render a persistent, non-dismissible admin dashboard warning (RTL/FA+EN, `role="alert"`) listing open unmatched and reversal-failed chargebacks.
- Fix: write the outbox row and its `notification_job` rows in one explicit transaction. On idempotency conflict, load the existing outbox id and upsert the required jobs so a retry after a partial failure cannot permanently drop the alert.

- [x] Reversal-failed (`unresolved`) chargebacks alert finance the same way; successfully reversed chargebacks do not.
- [x] Duplicate provider event ids do not create a second outbox row (unique idempotency key per event + recipient).
- [x] Admin dashboard shows a warning while unmatched/unresolved rows exist, and hides it when the count is zero.

title: feat(wallet): detect provider chargebacks and map them to the original top-up (T-04.2.04.02)
body:
## What
- Adds HMAC-authenticated `POST /api/wallet/top-ups/chargeback` that parses inbound provider chargeback/reversal notifications with the same signed-content scheme as online top-up callbacks.
- Maps a unique Completed online top-up credit by merchant order id (credit idempotency key / `pendingTransactionId`), then provider capture ref, then authority. A present stronger locator that does not uniquely amount-match does not fall through.
- Authority matching reads `metadata.authority` then `metadata.gateway.authority`; `refId` is an authority-compatible fallback only when no stored authority exists, so an authority-only notification still maps when the credit's `refId` is a distinct provider capture ref.
- When mapped, calls `WalletService.reverseTransaction` so the original Completed credit is left untouched and a compensating `reversal` row posts. Duplicate event ids replay the stored outcome. If the original is already reversed, the event is recorded as reversed without inserting a second ledger row.
- When untraceable, persists a durable `wallet_chargeback_events` row as `unmatched` (general exception) without debiting an unknown wallet. When mapped but the reversal cannot post (insufficient available balance), the event is `unresolved` so finance alerting (T-04.2.04.03) can pick it up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Parse inbound notification — verified: `parseChargebackNotificationJson` accepts `chargeback` / `reversed` / `reversal`, merchant id, positive IRR amount, and locators; rejects invalid JSON, types, amounts, and non-UUID order ids (`packages/shared` + API unit tests).
- [x] Validate signature — verified: missing secret → 503; tampered HMAC → 401 before any mapping/reversal; replay window → 401; merchant mismatch → 401. Integration test proves a wrong secret never writes `wallet_chargeback_events`.
- [x] Map to original top-up — verified: unique Completed credit matched by pending order id first, then provider ref, then authority; amount mismatch / ambiguity / wrong type or state → unmatched. Real PostgreSQL test posts a reversal against the original credit and leaves that credit `Completed`.
- [x] Authority-only mapping with a distinct provider ref — verified: `topUpAuthority` prefers stored metadata authority over `refId`; service and real-PostgreSQL tests reverse a credit whose `refId` is a non-null capture ref different from `metadata.authority`.
- [x] Compensating transaction, not history rewrite — verified: original top-up row stays Completed; reversal posts the opposite amount via `reverseTransaction`.
- [x] Untraceable chargeback is a general exception — verified: unmatched event stored with null original/wallet FKs and no extra ledger rows.
- [ ] Finance alert (push + dashboard) — not this task; owned by T-04.2.04.03. Unmatched/unresolved events are persisted for that follow-up.

title: feat(wallet): implement reverseTransaction compensating ledger reversal (T-04.2.04.01)
body:
## What
- Adds `WalletService.reverseTransaction(originalTransactionId, reason, idempotencyKey)` to post a Completed `reversal` ledger row with the opposite signed amount and adjust `posted_balance` in the same transaction.
- The original row is never rewritten: history stays immutable and `postedBalance = SUM(Completed amounts)` still holds.
- Unique `reverses_transaction_id` (migration 0074) plus the existing idempotency key prevent double-reversal and make retries safe.
- Reversing a credit requires `availableBalance >= original.amount`; reversing a debit credits the wallet. Reservations, reversals, and non-Completed rows are refused.

- [x] Same idempotency key retries return the original reversal and do not double-adjust (unit + real PostgreSQL tests, including concurrent same-key retries).
- [x] A second reversal of the same original (different key) is rejected; concurrent distinct-key races leave exactly one reversal.
- [x] Insufficient available balance, missing original, reservation/reversal types, and non-Completed states are rejected and leave the wallet unchanged.

title: test(wallet): concurrent payInvoiceWithWallet races (T-04.2.03.04)
body:
## What
- Add a real-PostgreSQL integration suite for `payInvoiceWithWallet` concurrency (T-04.2.03.04).
- Concurrent distinct-key payments of one invoice: exactly one succeeds and debits once; the others fail with already-paid.
- Concurrent same-key retries all fulfill: exactly one `replayed: false`, the other two `replayed: true`, and all three share the same transaction ID and Paid result. A sequential duplicate key is a replay; the same key on a different invoice is a collision.
- Insufficient availableBalance — including reserved funds consuming posted, and concurrent short-balance attempts — rolls wallet, invoice, ledger, and audit back.
- Two invoices racing for funds that cover only one remaining amount: one settles Paid, the other fails, one ledger row. When funds cover both remainings, both settle Paid.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Concurrent payment attempts (one succeeds, others fail) — three distinct-key payments of one invoice: 1 fulfilled Paid, 2 `ConflictException` already-paid, one wallet_transactions row, one audit row, postedBalance reduced once.
- [x] Duplicate idempotency key — three concurrent same-key retries all fulfill (no `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`); exactly one `replayed: false` and two `replayed: true`; all three share one transaction ID and Paid result; sequential retry returns `replayed: true`; reusing the key on a different invoice 409s and leaves that invoice Unpaid.
- [x] Insufficient balance — sequential and concurrent short-balance attempts throw `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, including when reserved funds leave available below remaining; wallet/invoice/ledger/audit unchanged.
- [x] Race conditions — two invoices on one wallet with funds for only one remaining: exactly one Paid; with funds for both remainings: both Paid and postedBalance equals start minus the sum.

title: feat(wallet): implement payInvoiceWithWallet remaining debit (T-04.2.03.01)
body:
## What

body:
## What
- Adds a worker cron that auto-rejects **online** wallet top-ups still in `Pending` after the default 30-minute TTL (`ONLINE_TOPUP_PENDING_TTL_MS`).
- Rejection only advances the intent to `Rejected` and stamps `metadata.expiry`; posted/reserved balances are unchanged, and bank-receipt Pendings are ignored.
- Provider authority stays on the row so a later authenticated callback can still credit (TTL expiry is reconcilable, not a terminal staff reject).
- Wires the job as `online_topup_expiry_scan` on a one-minute cadence (`ONLINE_TOPUP_EXPIRY_SCAN_MS`), with lock/re-check, bounded drain, and failure isolation matching the other wallet/invoice scanners.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Worker cron auto-rejects online `topup` rows stuck in `Pending` beyond the TTL (exclusive cutoff on `created_at`).
- [x] Bank-receipt Pending rows are not expired.
- [x] Wallet balances are not mutated; only ledger state + expiry metadata change.
- [x] Gateway authority is preserved so a later paid callback can still credit a TTL-`Rejected` intent.
- [x] Re-runs are idempotent; concurrent callback/worker races re-check under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
- [x] Job type is recorded for the failed-jobs dashboard (`online_topup_expiry_scan`).

## Validation

title: feat(wallet): admin-configurable versioned onlineTopUpLimit (T-04.2.02.06)
body:
## What
- Persist and read `onlineTopUpLimit` as versioned `app_config` (`finance.wallet_top_up_limit`): admin writes bump the per-key version, the global config version, and invalidate the config cache.
- Enforce the current ceiling at online top-up submission inside the Pending-row transaction. The enforced `{ onlineTopUpLimit, configVersion }` is snapshotted onto the ledger metadata.
- Serialize submission and admin-update even when the config row does not yet exist: both paths take the same `pg_advisory_xact_lock` before `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` / upsert, so a first admin write cannot commit a tighter ceiling after a submission has already observed the default.
- Idempotent retries of an already-accepted Pending row keep the original ceiling after a later admin tighten; new submissions use the new version.
- Admin UI (number input with grouped IRR formatting, Toman preview, and a future-top-ups warning) on the wallet receipts page. Customer wallet GET now returns `onlineTopUpLimit` so the top-up form can show the cap and fail closed client-side.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Admin-configurable `onlineTopUpLimit` with default 2,000,000,000 IRR — GET/PUT `/api/admin/config/wallet-top-up-limit`; missing rows serve the default at version `0`.
- [x] Versioned config — `app_config.version` increments on write, global `config_version` is bumped, and `ConfigCache.invalidate` runs after commit.
- [x] Enforced at submission — `OnlineTopUpService.initiate` re-reads the locked config before INSERT; amounts above the current ceiling are rejected with 400 and no ledger row.
- [x] Absent-row/first-write race is serialized — submission and admin update share `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(namespace), hashtext(key))` so `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` locking nothing cannot admit an over-limit Pending after a concurrent first write. Covered by a real-PostgreSQL concurrency test.
- [x] Retry with reduced amount — a later, lower limit applies to new submissions; in-flight Pending rows can be replayed with the original idempotency key.

title: feat(wallet): credit bank-receipt overpayment excess to the wallet (T-04.2.02.05)
body:
## What
- Staff can apply a bank-receipt confirmation to an invoice. The invoice is settled only up to remaining (`paid_amount` never exceeds `total_amount`); any excess is posted as a **separate** verified wallet credit via `WalletService.credit()` with its own idempotency key (`wallet-bank-receipt-overpayment-credit:<pendingId>`).
- After a positive allocation in the same transaction, the invoice takes the documented ConfirmBankReceipt path: **Unpaid / PartiallyFunded** first SubmitBankReceipt into PaymentUnderReview, then ConfirmBankReceipt to **Paid** (and `paid_at`) when the post-allocation amount covers `total_amount`, or **PartiallyFunded** otherwise.
- Invoice-linked confirmation of an **Overdue** invoice is rejected with 409. Overdue remains cancellable only; this PR does not add Overdue → PaymentUnderReview.
- Wallet-only confirmation (no invoice) is unchanged: the full receipt still credits the wallet through the existing top-up key.
- Staff review UI accepts an optional invoice ID, previews remaining vs excess, and FA/EN copy explains that over-settlement is forbidden.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] If receipt amount > invoice remaining, excess is credited to the wallet as a distinct ledger row (not invoice over-settlement). Verified with unit and real-PostgreSQL integration tests.
- [x] Invoice allocation is capped at remaining (`min(receipt, remaining)`); `ck_paid_not_exceeds_total` is respected. Exact-remaining receipts do not call `WalletService.credit()`.
- [x] Overpayment credit uses a separate idempotency key from the wallet-top-up credit so retries cannot double-credit. Confirm retries do not bump `paid_amount` again.
- [x] Invoice must belong to the same profile as the wallet; mismatch is 409. Confirm + invoice allocation + state transition + excess credit + audit share one DB transaction (audit failure rolls back paid amount, state, and wallet).
- [x] Staff UI (RTL/FA+EN) shows remaining, invoice allocation, and excess before confirm.
- [x] Full allocation from Unpaid/PartiallyFunded transitions the invoice to Paid and sets `paid_at` through ConfirmBankReceipt. Partial allocation transitions to PartiallyFunded and leaves `paid_at` unset. Verified in PostgreSQL integration tests.
- [x] Overdue invoices cannot SubmitBankReceipt. Invoice-linked confirmation against Overdue returns 409, leaves paid amount/state unchanged, and does not credit the wallet. Verified in unit and PostgreSQL integration tests.

title: feat(wallet): bank receipt top-up stays Pending until finance confirms (T-04.2.02.03)
body:
## What
- Customers can top up a profile wallet by submitting a bank receipt: amount, payment date, payer/tracking reference, attachment, and optional note.
- `POST /api/wallet/:profileId/bank-receipt-top-ups` validates the payload (positive IRR with **no online limit**, real calendar date not in the future, recorded `uploads/document|image` attachment) and inserts a `topup` ledger row in **Pending** state.
- Posted and reserved balances are unchanged. Credit is deferred to staff confirmation (`T-04.2.02.04`). Idempotent retries reuse the matching Pending row.
- Wallet page adds an RTL-aware receipt form that uploads via the existing presigned-url / verify / record flow, then submits the Pending top-up.
- Review fix: the API returns the Pending amount as a decimal string so int8 values above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` match the ledger.
- Review fix: the same DB transaction that inserts the Pending row locks `storage_records` and transitions an `active` receipt to `immutable`.
- Review fix: recording an upload now re-verifies object bytes and persists `verified`, `uploadedBy`, `profileId`, and `purpose` in storage metadata. Submit requires a verified `bank_receipt` owned by the actor or bound to the accessible profile (unverified, wrong-owner, and wrong-purpose keys are rejected).
- Review fix: `receipt_attachment_key` is uniquely constrained so one stored receipt can back at most one top-up; reuse is allowed only for the same idempotency key. Concurrent different-key submissions of the same attachment insert exactly one Pending row.

title: feat(wallet): credit online top-ups from authenticated provider callbacks (T-04.2.02.02)
body:
## What
- HMAC-authenticated `POST /api/wallet/top-ups/callback` still verifies signature, ±5 minute replay window, merchant context, and credits via `WalletService.credit()` with idempotency key `wallet-online-topup-credit:<pendingId>`.
- ZarinPal GET returns on `GET /api/wallet/top-ups/callback` bind `orderId`/`Authority`/`Status` to the stored Pending top-up, call `PaymentGateway.verifyPayment()`, then credit with the same order-derived idempotency key.
- ZarinPal event ids now include the terminal status (`zarinpal-return:<orderId>:<authority>:<paid|cancelled|failed>`), so a browser `Status=NOK` cannot claim the same event as a later `Status=OK`.
- A terminal `unpaid` claim for the same pending order is reopened when a later `paid` delivery arrives, so an earlier unpaid finalize cannot suppress `verifyPayment`. Duplicate credits remain blocked by `WalletService.credit()` idempotency.
- A GET without ZarinPal params is still acknowledged and does not credit. Query params alone are never treated as proof of payment.
- Provider `event_id` is claimed **before** gateway verify, wallet credit, or pending-state mutations (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Provider callback verifies signature (HMAC-SHA256 `v1,<base64>` over `eventId.timestamp.rawBody` for signed POST)
- [x] Replay window rejects timestamps older/newer than ±5 minutes on signed POST
- [x] Event id is the replay/idempotency boundary: claimed atomically before side effects; ZarinPal GET uses a derived event id from `orderId` + `Authority` + terminal status
- [x] Merchant context is checked (configured merchant id on POST; pending order id, amount, and stored authority on both paths)
- [x] Credit is applied via `WalletService.credit()` with a stable order-derived idempotency key
- [x] Browser redirect query params are not treated as proof of payment; ZarinPal GET credits only after server-side `verifyPayment()`
- [x] Review finding: a prior ZarinPal `Status=NOK` no longer suppresses a later `Status=OK` for the same order and authority (distinct event ids + unpaid-to-paid reprocessing; regression covered in unit and PostgreSQL integration tests)

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api test` — pass (144 files, 2054 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db test` — pass (55 files, 446 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (32 files, 465 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n test` — pass (no test files)

## Risks / limitations
- ZarinPal GET has no HMAC timestamp; authenticity is the stored authority binding plus `verify.json`. Replay of the same return is gated by the status-scoped event id and the credit idempotency key.
- Signed POST still requires `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The ZarinPal GET path does not, because ZarinPal does not send that HMAC.
- A crash after the `processing` claim but before credit is recovered on the next delivery of the **same** event id and pending order.
- The original Pending top-up row is `Released` after credit so ledger reconciliation does not double-count; posted balance is the Completed `WalletService.credit()` row only.
- A browser NOK still marks the Pending row Failed; a later OK recovers that Failed row after server-side verify.

title: feat(wallet): implement WalletService.reserve and release for payment holds (T-04.2.01.05)
body:
## What
- `WalletService.reserve(walletId, amount, idempotencyKey, ref?)` holds funds for the payment flow: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, reject when `availableBalance` is below `amount`, increment `reserved_balance` under version + available-balance predicates (`version += 1`), and insert a Reserved ledger row (`type = reservation`, positive amount). Posted balance is unchanged.
- `WalletService.release(reservationId)` drops the hold: lock the reservation row, decrement `reserved_balance` under version + `reserved_balance >= amount`, and advance that row to Released. Re-release is idempotent and does not decrement twice.
- After T-04.2.01.02/04 locked `wallet_id` as UUID and bound debit to the wallet row's canonical `profile_id`, reserve/release still mixed caller-supplied ids into later mutations. Reserve now applies `::bigint` and binds the reserved-balance UPDATE plus ledger INSERT to canonical `profile_id`. Release binds the wallet UPDATE and the Reserved→Released ledger UPDATE to the locked row ids (`wallet.profile_id` and `reservation.id`), and refuses a concurrent state change if that ledger UPDATE matches no row.
- Mixed-case UUID callers reserve and release once against the stored ids. Same-key reserve retries still return the live Reserved row; colliding keys and a released key still raise ConflictException.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `reserve(walletId, amount)` checks `availableBalance >= amount`, increments `reservedBalance` (not `postedBalance`), and inserts a Reserved ledger row with a positive amount (unit + real PostgreSQL). `idempotencyKey` is required because ledger rows cannot omit it.
- [x] `release(reservationId)` decrements `reservedBalance`, leaves `postedBalance` unchanged, and marks the reservation Released. Re-release is idempotent.
- [x] Reserve UPDATE/INSERT and release wallet/ledger UPDATEs use the locked row canonical UUIDs (uppercase `walletId` / `reservationId` unit and integration tests).
- [x] Idempotent reserve retry with the same key/amount/refId returns the original Reserved row and does not double-hold, including concurrent same-key retries.
- [x] Concurrent distinct-key reserves both post when funds suffice; concurrent over-reserve lets exactly one succeed. Concurrent releases of the same hold decrement once.
- [x] Insufficient available balance (including when reserved funds consume posted) is BadRequest and writes no ledger row.
- [x] Colliding idempotency keys (credit, debit, different amount/refId, other wallet, already Released) raise ConflictException and do not mutate the wallet.
- [x] Missing wallet / missing reservation is NotFound. Non-reservation ledger rows and non-Reserved/non-Released states are Conflict. Non-positive amount and blank ids are BadRequest before opening a transaction.

## Validation
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — passed (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)

title: feat(wallet): restore credit postedBalance >= 0 optimistic update (T-04.2.01.03)
body:
## What
- `WalletService.credit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` already inserted a Completed ledger row and bumped `postedBalance` under optimistic locking. T-04.2.01.06 later dropped `AND posted_balance >= 0` from that UPDATE.
- Credit now posts through `applyPostedBalanceDelta(..., { requireNonNegativePostedBalance: true })`, so the UPDATE is `SET posted_balance = posted_balance + amount, version = version + 1 WHERE profile_id = X AND version = expectedVersion AND posted_balance >= 0`.

title: feat(wallet): initiate online top-up with limit check and gateway redirect (T-04.2.02.01)
body:
## What
- Add `POST /api/wallet/:profileId/top-ups` to start an online wallet top-up for the authenticated profile.
- Enforce the admin-configured per-transaction `onlineTopUpLimit` (`finance.wallet_top_up_limit`, default 2,000,000,000 IRR) **before** inserting a ledger row.
- Insert a `topup` wallet transaction in **Pending** state with channel metadata; `postedBalance` and `reservedBalance` are unchanged.
- Start a payment-gateway session and return `redirectUrl` so the customer can complete checkout. The wallet is **not** credited here — that remains T-04.2.02.02 (authenticated provider callback).
- Serialize gateway initialization per idempotency key: session advisory lock, Pending-row `FOR UPDATE`, atomic initializing claim, then compare-and-set persist of `metadata.gateway` + `ref_id`. Concurrent same-key retries call `startPayment` once and keep authority/ref_id aligned.
- Do not overwrite an existing initializing claim. Persist the provider idempotency key (Pending transaction id) and a per-transaction callback URL (`orderId`) on the claim.
- After an ambiguous `startPayment` failure (timeout, abort, 5xx), **keep** the initializing claim. Retry reconciles through `recoverPayment` and never calls `startPayment` again, so a provider session created before the client timed out cannot be replaced by a second authority. A definite provider rejection still releases the claim.
- Production adapters demonstrate recovery, not just an `Idempotency-Key` header: ZarinPal inquires `unVerified` and matches amount plus the unique callback URL; the HTTP adapter GETs an inquiry URL keyed by `orderId` / idempotency key. The local redirect adapter reuses its deterministic authority.
- Register a real PSP adapter: ZarinPal v4 (merchant-authenticated payment request) or a generic HTTP JSON PSP. The redirect builder is only `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ADAPTER=redirect` and is refused when `NODE_ENV=production` if merchant/API credentials are missing.
- Resolve the PSP callback URL from the factory's supplied environment. Production fails application startup unless `API_PUBLIC_URL` or `APP_PUBLIC_URL` is an explicit public HTTPS origin (not localhost or an IP, no credentials). Development may omit both and uses `http://localhost:4000`.
- Parse provider-supplied and configured gateway redirect/start URLs and accept only HTTPS destinations whose host is on the allow-list (`PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_HOSTS` plus hosts from configured request/start URLs). Credentials, unsupported schemes, and unexpected hosts are rejected. The wallet page also refuses to `window.location.assign` a non-HTTPS URL.
- Idempotent retries with the same key reuse the original Pending row and redirect; a colliding key with a different amount is 409. Over-limit submissions can retry with a reduced amount.
- Pending ledger inserts bind to the locked wallet row's canonical `profile_id` (mixed-case UUID replay), matching credit/debit/reserve.
- Customer `/wallet` page collects an IRR amount, posts with an `Idempotency-Key`, and redirects the browser to the gateway. Persian/English copy and RTL are included.
- Normalize Persian (`۰`–`۹`) and Arabic-Indic (`٠`–`٩`) numerals to ASCII before filtering/parsing the top-up amount so localized keyboards can complete the journey.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Limit is validated at submission via `WalletService.validateOnlineTopUpAmount` / `isOnlineWalletTopUpAllowed` (default 2e9 IRR, persisted admin limit, and `0` kill switch). Verified by unit and PostgreSQL integration tests.
- [x] A successful initiation creates a Pending `topup` ledger row and does not change wallet balances. Verified against real PostgreSQL.
- [x] The API returns a gateway `redirectUrl`; the wallet page assigns `window.location` to it only after HTTPS/no-credentials checks. Credit is deferred to the callback handler.
- [x] Over-limit amounts are rejected with 400 and no ledger insert; the UI tells the customer to retry with a smaller amount.
- [x] Idempotent retry returns the same Pending transaction and redirect; a different amount on the same key is conflict.
- [x] Mixed-case wallet UUID spellings reuse the same Pending row and insert against the canonical `profile_id`.
- [x] Concurrent same-key retries invoke `startPayment` once; stored `metadata.gateway.authority` matches `ref_id`. Verified by a delayed-PSP PostgreSQL integration test.
- [x] Production adapter posts amount/order/callback to the provider, validates the response, and returns the provider-issued authority and redirect URL. Redirect builder is explicit non-production only; missing production credentials fail factory startup.
- [x] Production factory startup fails when the callback origin is missing, malformed, HTTP, localhost, an IP, or includes credentials; a valid public HTTPS origin is accepted. Verified by unit tests against the factory-supplied env.
- [x] Provider redirect URLs and configured start URLs must be HTTPS hosts on the gateway allow-list; javascript/data/http/credentialed/off-allow-list responses are rejected. Verified by malicious redirect-response tests.
- [x] Persian and Arabic-Indic numerals entered on the Persian/RTL wallet form are normalized to ASCII and submitted as the IRR amount. Verified by WalletPage tests.
- [x] After `startPayment` succeeds, a database error or crash before persist leaves the initializing claim; a retry recovers via provider inquiry and does not call `startPayment` again or create a second payable session. Verified by unit and PostgreSQL integration tests.
- [x] When the provider creates a session but the client receives a timeout, the initializing claim is kept; retry recovers that authority and cannot create a second one. Verified by unit, HTTP/ZarinPal adapter, and PostgreSQL integration tests.

## Validation
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (32 files, 465 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api test` — pass (140 files, 2019 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass

- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n test` — pass (no test files; `--passWithNoTests`)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api lint` / `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web lint` — not available (packages have no lint script)

- Production requires `API_PUBLIC_URL` or `APP_PUBLIC_URL` as a public HTTPS origin, plus `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_MERCHANT_ID` (ZarinPal) or `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ADAPTER=http` with `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_REQUEST_URL` + `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_API_KEY`. Checkout hosts other than the request/start URL hosts must be listed in `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

If inquiry finds no unique matching session, retry returns 502 and does not start a second payment; the Pending row waits for expiry (T-04.2.02.07) or a later successful recover.

title: feat(wallet): scheduled ledger vs balance reconciliation worker (T-04.2.01.08)
body:
## What
- Adds a scheduled worker (`wallet_reconciliation_scan`) that compares each wallet's cached `posted_balance` / `reserved_balance` to the immutable ledger: posted = SUM of Completed amounts, reserved = SUM of Reserved amounts.
- On drift, inserts an `open` `wallet_mismatch` row into `reconciliation_exceptions` (finance queue) with severity, description, and JSONB details. Wallets already on the queue (`open` / `investigating`) are not duplicated.
- Re-checks under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` so an in-flight credit/debit is not reported as mismatch. Cadence is hourly (`WALLET_RECONCILIATION_SCAN_MS`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Scheduled reconciliation worker compares ledger sum vs wallet cached balances — candidate SQL uses `SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE state = Completed|Reserved)` vs `posted_balance` / `reserved_balance`; proven by unit tests and Testcontainers integration tests.
- [x] Mismatch is reported to the finance queue — inserts `reconciliation_exceptions` with `exception_type=wallet_mismatch`, `status=open`, and details including `walletId` and deltas; matching wallets and Pending-only ledgers are not reported.
- [x] Repeating ticks do not flood the queue — already-queued wallets are excluded via `details.walletId`; a second pass reports 0 new rows.
- [x] Worker is wired into the background process with job-recorder success/failure (`wallet_reconciliation_scan` added to `BACKGROUND_JOB_TYPES`).

## Validation

- PostgreSQL evaluates the derived available-balance expression on INSERT/UPDATE. `available_balance` is not a stored column and is not a generated STORED column (this stack is PostgreSQL 16; VIRTUAL generated columns are PG 18+).

- [x] Enforcement is on the derived value, not a stored column — `information_schema.columns` has no `available_balance`; no generated columns (`attgenerated`); migration has no `GENERATED ALWAYS AS` / trigger / `ADD COLUMN available_balance`.

title: feat(wallet): implement WalletService.reserve and release for payment holds (T-04.2.01.05)
body:
## What
- Implement `WalletService.reserve(walletId, amount, idempotencyKey, ref?)` and `WalletService.release(reservationId)` for the payment-hold flow.
- In one DB transaction, `reserve` locks the wallet, rejects when `availableBalance` (`posted - reserved`) is below `amount`, increments `reserved_balance` under the optimistic `version` predicate plus `(posted_balance - reserved_balance) >= amount`, and inserts a `reservation` ledger row in state `Reserved` (positive amount). Posted balance is unchanged, so available balance falls by the hold.
- Retrying the same idempotency key returns the original ledger row only when it is the same live reservation (matching wallet, type, amount, refId, and `Reserved`). Credits, debits, released rows, and same-key parameter mismatches throw `ConflictException` on both the lookup path and unique-index race recovery.
- `release(reservationId)` locks the reservation then the wallet, decrements `reserved_balance` under `version` + `reserved_balance >= amount`, and advances the row to `Released`. Posted balance is unchanged. Re-release is idempotent and does not decrement twice. Non-reservation rows and non-`Reserved`/`Released` states throw `ConflictException`; a missing id throws `NotFoundException` (rolled back, not committed-then-thrown).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `reserve(walletId, amount)` exists for the payment flow. Ledger uniqueness still requires an `idempotencyKey` (and optional ref), matching `credit`/`debit` and existing callers.
- [x] Available balance is checked as `postedBalance - reservedBalance`; insufficient funds (including reserved consumption) throw `BadRequestException` and write no ledger row.
- [x] A successful reserve increases `reservedBalance` and version by 1 and leaves `postedBalance` unchanged; the ledger row is type `reservation`, state `Reserved`, positive amount.
- [x] An existing idempotency key is accepted only for the same live reservation; credit/debit reuse, released-key replay, and same-key parameter mismatches throw `ConflictException` without mutating the wallet (lookup and unique-index recovery).
- [x] Concurrent distinct reserves that together exceed available balance: exactly one succeeds.
- [x] `release(reservationId)` drops `reservedBalance`, leaves `postedBalance` unchanged, and marks the reservation `Released`. Re-release and concurrent double-release decrement once.
- [x] Unit and real-PostgreSQL integration tests cover happy path, insufficient funds, idempotency, collision mismatches, concurrency, missing wallet/reservation, and non-reservation release.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/wallet/wallet.service.test.ts src/wallet/wallet-reserve.integration.test.ts src/wallet/wallet-credit.integration.test.ts src/wallet/wallet-debit.integration.test.ts` — pass (124 tests)

- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)

## Risks / limitations
- `reserve` keeps a required `idempotencyKey` beyond the two-argument epic signature because `wallet_transactions.idempotency_key` is `NOT NULL` unique; callers already pass the key.
- Release records the unhold by advancing the original reservation to `Released` rather than inserting a separate `type=release` ledger row. Reconciliation (T-04.2.01.08) should treat `reservedBalance` as the sum of `Reserved` rows.
- The nonnegative available-balance DB trigger/CHECK is still T-04.2.01.07; reserve/release enforce available and reserved balances in application logic and SQL `WHERE` predicates.

title: feat(wallet): implement WalletService.credit with collision-safe idempotency
body:
## What
- `WalletService.credit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` remains a single DB transaction: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, insert a Completed `wallet_transactions` ledger row (positive IRR amount, canonical wallet UUID), then `UPDATE posted_balance` with `WHERE version = X AND posted_balance >= 0`.
- Idempotent retries now replay only the same Completed credit (matching type, amount, and `refId`). Collisions with a debit, reservation, or a different credit command throw `ConflictException` and do not mutate the wallet — including the unique-index race recovery path.
- Ledger inserts use the wallet row's canonical `profile_id` so UUID spelling variants cannot store a non-canonical `wallet_id`.
- Two API tests whose `2026-09-01` fixtures are no longer in the future were advanced so the affected-package CI suite stays green on this date.

- [x] Duplicate `idempotencyKey` for the same credit command returns the original transaction and does not credit twice, including concurrent retries.
- [x] Retrying the same key with uppercase vs lowercase spellings of the same wallet UUID returns the original ledger row and does not change the balance.
- [x] A colliding idempotency key owned by another wallet, a debit/reservation, or a different credit (amount/type/refId) is rejected without mutating the wallet.
- [x] Concurrent distinct keys both post; final `posted_balance` equals the sum.
- [x] Negative `posted_balance` rejects the credit and writes no ledger row.

title: feat(wallet): implement WalletService.debit reserve-then-complete (T-04.2.01.04)
body:
## What
- Implement `WalletService.debit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` with the same locking/idempotency shape as `credit`.
- In one DB transaction: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, reject when `availableBalance` (`posted - reserved`) is below `amount`, atomically reserve (`reserved_balance += amount` under `version` + available predicate) then complete (`posted_balance -= amount`, `reserved_balance -= amount`), and insert a Completed ledger row with a negative amount.
- Retrying the same idempotency key returns the original ledger row only when it is the same Completed debit (matching type, negative amount, and refId). Credits, reservations, and same-key debits with different parameters throw `ConflictException` on both the lookup path and unique-index race recovery, so a mismatched ledger row is never reported as a successful debit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `debit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` exists with a dedicated `WalletDebitRef` (`payment` | `compensating` | `reversal`).
- [x] Available balance is checked as `postedBalance - reservedBalance`; insufficient funds (including reserved consumption) throw `BadRequestException` and write no ledger row.
- [x] Reserve then complete happens atomically in one transaction under optimistic version predicates; net `reservedBalance` is unchanged and `postedBalance` drops by `amount` (`version += 2`).
- [x] Ledger amount is negative, state is `Completed`, and the unique `idempotency_key` prevents double-debits (including concurrent same-key retries and UUID spelling variants).
- [x] An existing idempotency key is accepted only when it is a Completed negative debit for the same wallet, type, amount, and refId; credit/reservation reuse and same-key parameter mismatches throw `ConflictException` without mutating the wallet (verified on both lookup and unique-index recovery paths).
- [x] Concurrent distinct debits that together exceed available balance: exactly one succeeds.
- [x] Unit and real-PostgreSQL integration tests cover happy path, insufficient funds, idempotency, collision mismatches, concurrency, and missing wallet.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/wallet/wallet.service.test.ts` — pass (45 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/wallet/wallet-debit.integration.test.ts src/wallet/wallet-credit.integration.test.ts` — pass (22 tests, debit + credit real PostgreSQL)

- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)

## Risks / limitations

- The nonnegative available-balance DB trigger/CHECK is still T-04.2.01.07; debit enforces available balance in application logic and SQL `WHERE` predicates.
- Credit idempotency still accepts any same-wallet row; tightening that path is outside this debit task.

title: feat(wallet): implement WalletService.credit with versioned postedBalance
body:
## What
- Implement `WalletService.credit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` as a single DB transaction: lock the wallet (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), insert a Completed `wallet_transactions` ledger row (positive IRR amount), then update `posted_balance` with `WHERE version = X AND posted_balance >= 0`.
- Idempotent retries with the same key return the original ledger row and do not double-credit; a unique-index race on `idempotency_key` is mapped to the committed row (or 409 if the key belongs to another wallet).
- Ownership of an existing idempotency key is compared against the wallet row's canonical `profile_id`, so uppercase/lowercase UUID spellings of the same wallet retry without throwing ConflictException.
- Reject non-positive amounts, blank idempotency keys, non-credit ledger types, missing wallets, and wallets whose `posted_balance` is already negative.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `credit(walletId, amount, ref, idempotencyKey)` inserts a Completed ledger row and increments `posted_balance` + `version`.
- [x] The balance `UPDATE` uses `WHERE version = X AND posted_balance >= 0` (asserted in unit tests and enforced against real PostgreSQL).
- [x] Duplicate `idempotencyKey` returns the original transaction and does not credit twice, including concurrent retries.
- [x] Retrying the same key with uppercase vs lowercase spellings of the same wallet UUID returns the original ledger row and does not change the balance (review round 1).
- [x] Concurrent distinct keys both post; final `posted_balance` equals the sum.
- [x] Negative `posted_balance` rejects the credit and writes no ledger row.

title: feat(invoice): customer invoice details show original + correction chain (T-04.1.05.04)
body:
## What
- Customer-facing invoice details API (`GET /api/invoices/:invoiceId`) scoped to the active profile. The payload includes the original invoice and every linked replacement (`replacesInvoiceId`) or adjustment (`adjustmentForInvoiceId`), each with the staff-supplied explanation.
- `GET /api/invoices` plus `/invoices` list scaffolding so customers can reach details from the dashboard nav and unpaid-invoice card.
- Original + correction chain on `/invoices/$invoiceId` with RTL, FA/EN copy, and decimal-digit IRR amounts.
- Draft invoices are excluded from customer detail lookup and family-member queries (`state <> 'Draft'`), matching the list endpoint.
- Correction-family loading uses a recursive CTE with path-based cycle detection. Families longer than the old 50-hop walk are returned in full (safety diameter 256). If that bound is exhausted or the true original cannot be identified, the API returns an explicit 500 instead of a partial chain or a mislabeled `originalInvoiceId`.
- **Fix:** `resolveActiveProfileId` now excludes archived profiles (`AND archived = false`), matching the user-settings active-profile query. An archived default (or earliest archived fallback) no longer isolates customer invoice list/details; a user with only archived profiles receives the no-active-profile 404.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Customer invoice details page shows the original invoice together with linked replacements and adjustments.
- [x] Each linked correction/replacement includes the staff-supplied explanation of the change (from invoice metadata, with adjustment line text as fallback).
- [x] Invoices are isolated to the caller's active (non-archived) profile; other profiles 404 without leaking existence.
- [x] An archived default profile is skipped in favor of a non-archived profile; a user with only archived profiles receives the no-active-profile 404 on both customer invoice endpoints.
- [x] Draft invoices are not customer-visible: a direct draft request returns 404, and draft linked family members are excluded from the correction chain.
- [x] Amounts are serialized as decimal-digit IRR strings (no JSON Number / IEEE float).
- [x] FA/EN dictionaries and RTL layout are in place for the details page.
- [x] A valid family longer than 50 invoices keeps the true original and the complete linked chain (unit-tested with 51 replacements).
- [x] Exhausting the family safety bound, or failing to find a unique root, is an explicit error rather than a truncated or mis-rooted response.

title: feat(invoice): create linked post-payment adjustment invoices (T-04.1.05.03)
body:
## What
- `createAdjustmentInvoice(originalInvoiceId, amount, reason)` issues a linked post-payment adjustment. Positive amounts remain additional-charge Unpaid invoices; negative amounts are first-class credit notes.
- Credit readback returns persisted `payableFrom: null` (nullable on `CreateAdjustmentInvoiceResult` and the excerpt). Charge adjustments still require a non-null `payableFrom`.
- Migration 0067 is expand/migrate: nullable `adjustment_kind` + generated `accounting_amount`, deterministic backfill of existing linked rows (`metadata.kind` when charge/credit, otherwise `charge`), and the kind/link CHECK added as `NOT VALID`. VALIDATE is deferred until old writers are retired.
- Dashboard unpaid-invoice counts exclude credit notes. The state machine rejects `PayFromWallet`, `SubmitBankReceipt`, and `MarkOverdue` on credits so they cannot enter the normal payment flow.
- The paid original is never rewritten (only `metadata.adjustedByInvoiceIds`).
