title: feat(invoice): cancel and replace unpaid invoices with a linked replacement (T-04.1.05.02)
body:
## What
- Adds `CancelAndReplaceInvoiceService.cancelAndReplaceInvoice(invoiceId, reason, newLines)` for pre-payment invoice corrections (S-04.1.05).
- Validates a non-empty reason and `newLines`, locks the original, and rejects any confirmed payment (`paid_amount > 0`) or a state other than Draft / Unpaid / Overdue.
- Cancels the original via the invoice state machine (`invoice.cancel` audit + `cancelled_at`) and inserts a linked replacement with `replaces_invoice_id` set, staff-entered lines, and a calculation snapshot.
- Issues the replacement atomically (Draft → Unpaid) so the customer has a payable corrected invoice and the new lines are immutable. Origin FKs are copied; replacement `type` is `'manual'` because `newLines` are staff-entered.
- Rewrites `uq_invoices_order_id_type` as a partial unique index on ordinary invoices (`replaces_invoice_id IS NULL`) so a replacement can copy `order_id` without colliding with a cancelled original or a sibling ordinary `manual` invoice. Cancelled originals still occupy the ordinary uniqueness slot.
- Records `replacedByInvoiceId` on the original metadata. The whole cancel + insert + issue runs in one transaction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `cancelAndReplaceInvoice(invoiceId, reason, newLines)` exists and is registered on `InvoiceModule`.
- [x] No confirmed payment: `paid_amount > 0` is rejected with `ConflictException`; original row is unchanged.
- [x] Original is cancelled (state `Cancelled`, `cancelled_at` set, `invoice.cancel` audit) with the required reason.
- [x] Replacement is created with `replacesInvoiceId` pointing at the original, new lines, totals, and calculation snapshot.
- [x] Replacement is issued in the same transaction (Unpaid) so the customer has a payable corrected invoice.
- [x] Unpaid / Draft / Overdue (unpaid) originals are replaceable; Paid / PartiallyFunded / PaymentUnderReview / terminal states are rejected.
- [x] Empty reason and invalid lines fail before any write; audit-actor failure rolls back both cancel and replacement.
- [x] Order-linked original of type `manual` can be replaced without a unique-constraint error (real PostgreSQL).
- [x] Auto original whose order already has another ordinary `manual` invoice can be replaced without a unique-constraint error (real PostgreSQL).
- [x] Ordinary (non-replacement) `(order_id, type)` idempotency is preserved, including after the original is cancelled.
- [ ] Staff HTTP API / UI for this command — not in this task (customer chain UI is T-04.1.05.04; adjustment invoices are T-04.1.05.03).

title: feat(invoice): stop reminders when invoice enters Paid/Cancelled/Refunded (T-04.1.04.06)

title: feat(invoice): admin toggle UI for reminder offsets per service type (T-04.1.04.05)
body:
## What
- Add `invoice_reminder_offset_toggles` (migration 0062) so each canonical reminder offset (`-7`, `-3`, `-1`, `0`, `+1`, `+7`) can be enabled or disabled per service type (`electricity`, `saving_plan`, `consultation`, `manual`). Missing pairs default to enabled.
- Admin GET/PUT `/api/admin/config/invoice-reminder-offsets` (platform admin) upserts one toggle, writes an audit event, and returns the full 4×6 matrix.
- Admin Invoices page shows an RTL/accessible switch matrix (FA/EN) that persists each toggle immediately.
- ReminderScheduler reads the matrix each pass and omits disabled offsets for the invoice’s `metadata.due.serviceType`. Unclassified invoices keep the full canonical set.
- Fix: overlapping PUTs no longer replace or restore the entire matrix from a request-local snapshot. Pending state is tracked per cell; success/failure patches only that cell via functional updates.
- Fix: ReminderScheduler candidate selection excludes service types with no currently enabled offsets (`<> ALL($6)`). Fully disabled invoices stay unscheduled until a toggle is re-enabled, but they no longer occupy the bounded oldest-first window and starve later invoices of enabled types.
- Fix: concurrent first writes for the same `(serviceType, offset)` pair take a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` before reading the previous row. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` locks nothing when the row is absent, so two racing inserts could both record `previousEnabled=true`; the advisory lock serializes the pair so each audit event’s `previousEnabled` matches the immediately preceding committed value (default `true` when no row exists yet). Audit `created_at` uses `clock_timestamp()` so the trail orders by real write time.
- Fix: PUT is guarded by `StepUpGuard` and `@RequiresStepUp()`. Disabling an offset can suppress payment reminders for an entire service type, so a stolen or unattended admin session is not enough. The web matrix intercepts `AUTHZ:STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, prompts for the admin password (`POST /api/auth/step-up`), and retries the original PUT.
- Fix: `saveToggle` and `verifyStepUp` catch rejected fetch promises. A network failure on PUT reverts the optimistic cell, clears its pending key, and shows `admin.invoices.reminders.saveFailed`. A rejected step-up request keeps the challenge open, preserves queued items, and shows `admin.invoices.reminders.stepUp.failed`. A rejected retry PUT after successful step-up also reverts and surfaces the save failure.
- Fix: the step-up dialog traps Tab/Shift+Tab, marks the rest of the page `inert`, and restores focus to the initiating switch on Escape, cancel, and successful submit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Admin can enable/disable each of the six canonical offsets independently per service type (API + UI matrix of 24 switches).
- [x] Defaults match S-04.1.04: missing rows are treated as enabled.
- [x] ReminderScheduler omits disabled offsets when inserting `invoice_reminder_schedule` rows for newly issued invoices (unit + PostgreSQL integration tests).
- [x] FA/EN copy, RTL layout, labeled switches, and CSRF on the write path.
- [x] Toggles apply to newly scheduled invoices only; already-inserted schedule rows are left in place (cancel-on-paid remains T-04.1.04.06).
- [x] Rapid successive toggles on different cells keep the displayed matrix consistent with successful writes; a failed save reverts only the failed cell.
- [x] PUT requires a fresh step-up: `StepUpGuard` rejects `set` when `stepUpVerifiedAt` is null with `AUTHZ:STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, and allows it after a recent verification. GET/`list` does not require step-up.
- [x] The admin toggle UI handles `AUTHZ:STEP_UP_REQUIRED` with a password challenge, retries the PUT after `POST /api/auth/step-up`, and reverts on cancel or failed verification.
- [x] A fully disabled service type cannot starve later invoices: more than `DEFAULT_REMINDER_SCHEDULE_MAX_PAGES * batchSize` older electricity invoices with every offset off still allow a newer consultation invoice to be scheduled in the same pass; re-enabling an offset returns that type to the candidate set.
- [x] Concurrent first writes for the same pair produce a truthful audit chain: two racing disables of a missing `electricity/-7` row record `previousEnabled=true` then `previousEnabled=false`, matching the preceding committed value (PostgreSQL integration test).
- [x] A rejected PUT promise reverts the optimistic toggle, re-enables the switch, and shows the localized save-failed message (does not leave the cell permanently pending).
- [x] A rejected step-up fetch keeps the challenge open, preserves the queued toggle, and shows the localized verification-failed message so the admin can retry.
- [x] The step-up dialog traps Tab/Shift+Tab, marks background content inert, closes on Escape, and restores focus to the initiating switch on every close path (keyboard unit tests).

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/admin/reminder-offset-toggle.service.test.ts src/admin/reminder-offset-toggle.controller.test.ts src/admin/reminder-offset-toggle.service.integration.test.ts` — pass (12 tests, including step-up reject/allow and concurrent first-write audit chain)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web exec vitest run src/components/ReminderOffsetTogglePanel.test.tsx` — pass (17 tests, including Tab/Shift+Tab containment, Escape, inert background, and focus restoration on cancel/submit)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web test` — pass (58 tests, 7 files)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/i18n test` — pass (no test files)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api lint` — not available (package has no lint script)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/web lint` — not available (package has no lint script)
- Root `pnpm test` / `pnpm lint` — not run; package tests were run for the changed web package plus task-specific api tests

## Risks / limitations
- Disabling an offset does not cancel already-inserted `invoice_reminder_schedule` rows; those remain until they send or T-04.1.04.06 cancels them on Paid/Cancelled/Refunded.
- Invoices without `metadata.due.serviceType` keep every canonical offset (same as pre-toggle behavior) and are never excluded by the fully-disabled-type filter.
- Concurrent edits by two admins on different cells are still last-write-wins on the server; per-cell reconcile only keeps a single admin session’s UI consistent under overlapping requests. Same-cell first writes are now serialized for a truthful audit trail.
- Residual empty-plan invoices whose service type still has some enabled offsets (elapsed remaining offsets) can still occupy in-tick pagination; they are not a permanent zero-plan cohort because the SQL horizon and same-tick keyset already skip terminally stale rows.
- Advisory locks use `hashtext` of a namespaced pair; a theoretical hash collision with another two-int advisory lock is accepted as vanishingly unlikely for this 24-cell keyspace.
- The step-up challenge is implemented on this reminder-offset panel only. Other raw-fetch admin config panels still defer step-up until they gain the same flow.
- A step-up network failure reuses the password-failure copy (`stepUp.failed`) rather than a distinct offline message.
- Keyboard focus management was verified with jsdom unit tests, not a browser assistive-technology pass.

title: feat(invoice): ReminderSender hourly worker via outbox (T-04.1.04.03)
body:
## What
- Add `ReminderSender` (`sendDueInvoiceReminders`) as an hourly worker loop (`INVOICE_REMINDER_SEND_MS`, default 1h).
- Each tick claims due `invoice_reminder_schedule` rows (`status=scheduled`, `scheduled_at <= now`), grouped by `(invoiceId, offset)`.
- Re-locks the invoice and skips Paid / Cancelled / Refunded (and Draft); Overdue and in-flight payment states still send.
- Writes one `payment.invoice_reminder` notification-outbox event (in-app plus due email/sms) in the same transaction as `status=sent` / `sent_at`.
- Fold the outbox row `idempotency_key` into per-channel transport keys **only** for `payment.invoice_reminder` (`sha256(eventKey:channel:profileId:outboxKey)`), so two reminders for the same profile stay distinct at Resend/SMS.ir.
- Keep the legacy digest `sha256(eventKey:channel:profileId)` for every other event so a queued or retrying row created before this deploy cannot present a new provider key and redeliver.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Cron every hour picks due reminders — worker interval defaults to 3_600_000ms (`DEFAULT_REMINDER_SEND_INTERVAL_MS`); override via `INVOICE_REMINDER_SEND_MS`.
- [x] Checks invoice state before send — candidate SQL excludes stop states (`invoice_state[]`); lock re-check uses `isEligibleForReminderSend`.
- [x] Sends via outbox — `enqueueOutbox` with event key `payment.invoice_reminder`, idempotency `sha256(event:invoiceId:offset)`.
- [x] Does not send for Paid / Cancelled / Refunded — verified in unit and integration tests; future-row cancellation remains T-04.1.04.06.
- [x] Idempotent re-run — already-`sent` rows are not candidates; duplicate outbox keys still stamp schedule rows `sent`.
- [x] Distinct per-channel delivery keys for reminders — two reminder outbox rows for the same profile but different invoices/offsets produce distinct transport keys; retries of one row remain stable (dispatch test).
- [x] Legacy provider keys unchanged — a pre-existing non-reminder retry after deploy still hashes `eventKey:channel:profileId` (deploy-compat unit test).

## Validation
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (29 files, 438 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/worker typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/worker test` — pass (20 files, 219 tests, including ReminderSender unit + Testcontainers integration, reminder transport-key test, and legacy-retry deploy-compat test)

## Risks / limitations
- Unique `(invoiceId, offset, channel)` is T-04.1.04.04; this pass relies on outbox idempotency plus `status=sent`.
- Stop-state invoices are not marked `cancelled` here (T-04.1.04.06); they are skipped each hour until that task.
- If a group has only external channels due, `in_app` is prepended to satisfy the outbox contract (scheduler always inserts in-app at the same `scheduledAt`, so this is an edge case).
- Localized/versioned reminder templates are out of scope (E-05 template engine).
- The expanded per-channel digest is gated on `payment.invoice_reminder` (new event; no in-flight production rows). Other events keep the pre-existing formula.

title: feat(invoice): ReminderScheduler worker on invoice issue (T-04.1.04.02)
body:
## What
- Adds a `ReminderScheduler` worker that catch-up polls issued invoices with no `invoice_reminder_schedule` rows, computes reminder instants as `dueAt + offset` (canonical offsets `-7, -3, -1, 0, +1, +7`, exact 24-hour UTC days), snaps each instant into the daytime delivery window in the profile owner's timezone, and inserts one row per (offset, channel).
- Always schedules `in_app`; adds `email`/`sms` when those channels are enabled on `users.notification_preferences`.
- Idempotent without the later unique index: invoices that already have any schedule row are skipped, and each candidate is re-checked under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Paid/Cancelled/Refunded invoices are not scheduled (cancelling existing future rows is T-04.1.04.06).
- Registers `invoice_reminder_scheduler` as a background-job type and runs the pass on a 60s loop (`INVOICE_REMINDER_SCHEDULE_MS`).
- Fix (review round 1): a rejected `app_config` delivery-window query now aborts the pass with no inserts. Missing or malformed config still uses `loadDeliveryWindowConfig` normalization.
- Fix (review round 2): `planInvoiceReminders` takes `issuedAt` and a stable pass timestamp `now`. Offsets whose unsnapped instant predates issuance, or whose snapped `scheduledAt` is already behind `max(issuedAt, now - 1h)`, are omitted so ReminderSender cannot bulk-dispatch stale reminders after a short due period or a delayed catch-up poll. The 1h grace keeps the on-issue `-7` row of a default 7-day due period when the 60s poll is slightly late.
- Fix (review round 3): terminally stale invoices (latest possible reminder already outside the catch-up window) are excluded from the oldest-first candidate query, and a pass keyset-paginates past empty-plan pages in the same tick. A full batch of elapsed-offset invoices can no longer starve a newly issued invoice.
- Fix (review round 4): restore `MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS` to 3 and remove `test_fix_attempt_limit_allows_ten_rounds`. Raising the supervisor fix-round cap is unrelated to ReminderScheduler, contradicts AGENTS.md, and belongs in a separately scoped protocol task.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] On invoice issue (catch-up poll of issued invoices), compute reminder datetimes from `dueAt` plus the S-04.1.04 offsets and insert `invoice_reminder_schedule` rows — verified by worker unit tests (fake pool) and Testcontainers PostgreSQL integration tests (six `in_app` rows, idempotent re-run, stop states skipped).
- [x] Daytime window (default 09:00–21:00) applied in the profile timezone when computing `scheduledAt` — verified by `snapToDaytimeWindow` / `planInvoiceReminders` unit tests against Asia/Tehran boundaries.
- [x] `in_app` always plus enabled external channels — verified by preference parsing tests and a multi-channel INSERT assertion.
- [x] A rejected delivery-window configuration query produces no schedule inserts — verified by unit test (`connection reset` on `app_config`); absent config still schedules via `loadDeliveryWindowConfig` defaults.
- [x] Elapsed offsets are not queued: short due periods omit instants before `issuedAt`; delayed worker processing omits offsets already past `now` — verified by planner unit tests, fake-pool INSERT assertions, and a PostgreSQL integration test.
- [x] Terminally stale invoices cannot occupy the bounded candidate set and starve later issues — verified by candidate-query exclusion, in-pass pagination past a full empty-plan batch, and PostgreSQL tests that a newly issued invoice is scheduled after a full stale batch.
- [x] This PR does not weaken the supervisor three-round fix cap — `MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS` is 3; `test_fix_attempt_limit_allows_ten_rounds` is removed.
- [ ] Unique index on `(invoiceId, offset, channel)` — out of scope (T-04.1.04.04).
- [ ] Admin per-offset toggle per service type — out of scope (T-04.1.04.05).
- [ ] ReminderSender dispatch via outbox — out of scope (T-04.1.04.03).
- [ ] Cancel future rows on Paid/Cancelled/Refunded — out of scope (T-04.1.04.06); this task only skips those states when inserting a new plan.

## Validation
- `python3 -m unittest kanban.scripts.test_loop_runner -v` — pass (24 tests)
- `python3 kanban/scripts/build_backlog.py --check` — pass (1355 tasks, 116 traceability entries)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (29 files, 436 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/worker test` — pass (18 files, 196 tests, including ReminderScheduler unit + PostgreSQL integration)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/worker typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/api exec vitest run src/admin/failed-jobs.service.test.ts src/admin/failed-jobs.controller.test.ts` — pass (26 tests)

## Risks / limitations
- Scheduling is eventually consistent (default 60s poll), not in the issue transaction. Existing issued invoices without rows are backfilled on the next tick.
- Changing `dueAt` after issue does not rewrite already-inserted schedule rows (no unique-index upsert yet).
- Admin per-offset toggles are not consulted (T-04.1.04.05).
- A delivery-window query failure delays scheduling until the next successful tick; it no longer permanently locks in default hours.
- Missed offsets are dropped, not sent late. Invoices whose every offset has already elapsed are excluded from later candidate queries (and skipped if they still match the 8-day horizon).
- Catch-up grace is 1 hour: a worker delayed longer than that will omit the on-issue `-7` row of a 7-day due period rather than send it stale.
- A residual empty-plan cohort inside the 8-day horizon is paged past in the same tick, capped at 10 pages per pass.
- `main` already contains `MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS = 10` from PR #242. This branch restores the pre-#241 value of 3 so the ReminderScheduler three-dot diff no longer carries that protocol change; a later merge should keep `main`'s independently landed #242 unless that protocol change is reverted in its own task.

title: feat(invoice): mark past-due invoices Overdue via worker cron (T-04.1.03.04)
body:
## What
- Add a worker cron (`INVOICE_OVERDUE_SCAN_MS`, default 5 minutes) that marks invoices whose `dueAt` is strictly in the past and whose state is still `Unpaid` or `PartiallyFunded` as `Overdue`.
- Each mark stamps `overdue_at`, writes an `invoice.mark_overdue` audit row (`Marked overdue by cron`) in the same transaction, and uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` plus an eligibility re-check so a concurrent payment, cancel, or staff dueAt override cannot be overwritten.
- Register `invoice_overdue_scan` as a background job type so failures surface on the admin failed-jobs dashboard. No late fees; reminder sending stays with S-04.1.04.
- **Fix (review):** candidate SQL now compares `invoices.state` with `$1::invoice_state[]` (and the optimistic lock uses `$3::invoice_state`) so the scan is valid against the production enum. A Testcontainers integration test runs that query on the migrated invoice schema and proves `::text[]` raises operator `42883`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Cron/worker pass selects only `Unpaid` and `PartiallyFunded` invoices with `due_at IS NOT NULL AND due_at < now` (unit tests on the candidate SQL and eligibility helper; PostgreSQL integration test against `invoice_state`).
- [x] Matching invoices transition to `Overdue` with `overdue_at` set and an `invoice.mark_overdue` audit row (`fromState`, `toState`, reason, correlation id).
- [x] Draft, PaymentUnderReview, Paid, already Overdue, Cancelled, and refund states are not marked (eligibility helper + lock re-check tests + real-DB candidate query).
- [x] Re-run is a no-op for already-Overdue invoices; concurrent workers skip locked rows (`SKIP LOCKED`).
- [x] Per-invoice failure is isolated; the rest of the batch still runs.
- [x] No automatic late fee or reminder send in this task (S-04.1.03: continue reminders later; no auto-penalty in v1).
- [x] Candidate predicate is enum-compatible (`state = ANY($1::invoice_state[])`); the previous `$1::text[]` comparison is covered as a failing production query.

body:
Implements `04-invoices-wallet-contracts.md#T-04.1.02.07`.

## What

body:
Implements `04-invoices-wallet-contracts.md#T-04.1.02.03`.

## What
- **`AutoInvoiceService`** (`apps/api/src/invoice/auto-invoice.service.ts`) — the S-04.1.02 auto-generation seam: order/contract creation calls `createInvoiceForOrder(orderId, cmd)` to create a linked invoice ATOMICALLY in the same DB transaction.
  - **Tx join:** when the caller passes `client`, the service joins that open transaction (no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/release — the caller owns the lifecycle, mirroring `TransitionOptions.client`). Standalone use (no client) opens its own transaction.
  - **Snapshot semantics:** product price/title/type, resolved VAT rate (+ its resolution source), order terms (type, createdAt, dueAt) and gift-code discount are frozen at creation time in `invoices.metadata` AND in `invoice_items` (product composition table from T-04.1.02.01).
  - **Money rules:** all bigint IRR; VAT on the NET taxable amount (gift discount applied BEFORE VAT, T-03.02.03.06), half-up rounded per line via the existing `roundHalfUpDiv`.
  - **Atomic create+issue:** invoice (Draft) + lines + items + `Draft -> Unpaid` Issue transition + canonical `invoice.issue` audit entry in ONE transaction; a caller rollback drops the invoice too (integration-proven).
  - **Duplicate guard:** runtime check throws 409 if the order already has an auto invoice; the durable unique index is T-04.1.02.06.
  - Rejects: missing order/product (404), cancelled order, unpriced product, gift discount > line subtotal, dueAt in the past (400).
- **`auto-invoice.calculation.ts`** — pure, table-driven module: lineTotal = qty×unitPrice − discount, VAT half-up on net, invoice total; explicit error contract.

title: feat(invoice): ManualInvoiceService with atomic create+issue (T-04.1.02.02)
body:
Implements `04-invoices-wallet-contracts.md#T-04.1.02.02`.

## What
- **`ManualInvoiceService`** — finance staff create a manual invoice for a profile with N custom description+price lines (optionally linked to a contract); the system calculates `lineTotal`, per-line VAT (half-up rounded to the nearest IRR on taxable lines) and `totalAmount`, persists the Draft invoice + lines, and **issues it (Draft → Unpaid) in the same DB transaction** (sets `issuedAt`/`payableFrom`/`dueAt`, writes the canonical `invoice.issue` audit row).
- **Atomicity**: `InvoiceStateMachineService.transition()` now accepts `TransitionOptions.client` — a caller-owned transaction client — and then joins that transaction (no nested connect/BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/release). Money-moving create+issue flows stay atomic; the existing standalone path is unchanged.
- **Line ordering**: `invoice_lines.position` column (migration 0055) — explicit 0-based display order, the follow-up requested in the PR #223 review. Lines are written in staff entry order and read back `ORDER BY position`.
- **Idempotency**: optional `idempotencyKey` stored in invoice metadata, replayed inside the transaction (retry returns the existing invoice, no duplicate). Durable unique-index framework lands with C-04.CC.01.
- **Test-infra fix**: migration 0000 now takes a `pg_advisory_xact_lock` before `CREATE EXTENSION pgcrypto` — two API integration suites applying 0000 in parallel forks raced on `pg_extension_name_index` (intermittent `duplicate key value` suite failure).
- **Calculation snapshot**: creation inputs + rounding rule stored in `invoices.metadata` (formal `invoice_calculation_snapshot` column is T-04.1.02.08).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Staff can select a profile and add N custom lines (service command validates profile existence, ≥1 line, positive quantity, non-negative unit price, VAT rate 0..10000 bps)
- [x] System calculates totals — lineTotal = qty × unitPrice; VAT = roundHalfUp(lineTotal × rate / 10000) on taxable lines only; totalAmount = Σ(lineTotal + vatAmount)
- [x] Invoice is issued atomically with the creation (single BEGIN/COMMIT; rollback leaves no orphan Draft/lines/audit)
- [x] Issued invoice lands in `Unpaid` with issuedAt/payableFrom/dueAt (default due = issuedAt + 7 days pending T-04.1.03 config) and exactly one `invoice.issue` audit row
- [x] Optional contract link (`contractId`) supported

body:

## What
- New `invoice_lines` table (S-04.1.02 spec column set: `invoiceId`, `description`, `quantity`, `unitPrice`, `lineTotal`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `isTaxable`) — the priced display lines of an invoice, immutable once issued (corrections cancel+replace, S-04.1.05).

title: feat(admin): upload policy configuration — versioned per-category policies enforced against deployment limits (T-09.12.05)
body:
Implements `02-auth-users-admin.md#T-09.12.05`.

## What

Admin-configurable file upload policies, enforced at upload time within deployment-safe boundaries.

- **DB (migration 0050)** — `upload_policies`: versioned policy rows per canonical category (`document` | `image` | `video`). Per-row: lowercase `.ext` whitelist (CHECK 1..50 entries, each `^\.[a-z0-9]{1,10}$`), `max_size_bytes` (CHECK 1 B..100 MB), effective window (`effective_from` inclusive / `effective_until` exclusive, null = open), GIST EXCLUDE no-overlap per category (at most one open policy), `updated_at` trigger. Fully idempotent, mirrors migrations 0047/0049.
- **Admin API** — `api/admin/upload-policies`:
  - `GET` — list versioned policies, newest first, optional `?category=` filter, derived `current/scheduled/expired` status.
  - `POST` — create a new policy version: closes the previously open policy at the new `effectiveFrom`; re-submit of the identical open policy is a no-op (no audit); future-dated policies become `scheduled`. Policies are never mutated or hard-deleted — `POST :id/end` is the soft-close archival path (no-op when already ended).
  - Permission `admin:uploads:edit` (mapped to platform admin today per the S-09 convention), step-up required on all mutations, every mutation records a `change_recorded` audit event with request correlation id (single transaction).
  - **Deployment-safe boundaries at write time**: extensions must be a subset of the deployment-permitted extension set; `maxSizeBytes` must be ≤ the deployment per-category cap (itself ≤ 100 MB global hard cap). A policy can only *narrow* what the deployment allows.
- **Upload enforcement (both layers, "System enforces both DB config and deployment-level limits")** — new `UploadPolicyResolver` computes the effective policy as **min(DB policy, deployment config)**: extensions = DB whitelist ∩ deployment extension set (defense in depth; an intersect-empty policy fails closed), MIME set always the deployment set (never DB-widened), max size = min(DB, deployment cap). DB outage → logged fallback to the deployment baseline (baseline = pre-existing behavior; uploads don't freeze).
  - `POST api/upload/presigned-url` validates extension + claimed content type + size against the effective policy (referenced DB policy id / source echoed in rejection details).
  - **Detected content type**: new magic-byte sniffer (`content-type-sniffer.ts`, signature-based — PDF/JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP/AVIF/MP4/QuickTime/WebM/MKV/ZIP-OOXML/OLE2/gzip/tar/JSON/SVG/XML/text, with candidate lists for ambiguous containers) on the `POST api/upload/:key/verify` seam when the caller supplies `category`: object bytes are read back (≤ 4 KB) and compared to the effective policy's allowed MIME set → `confirmed` / `type_mismatch` (detected type + allowed set echoed). Legacy path without category keeps `pending_scan` (backward compatible).
  - New deployment `video` category (mp4/webm/mov/mkv, 100 MB) + `resolveCategory` video mapping.
- **Tests** (62 new): admin service (versioning, no-op, deployment-bound rejections, audit, PG-error mapping), admin controller (permission gate, zod payloads, UUID validation), sniffer (all signatures + ambiguity + junk-text rejection), resolver (intersection, min-size cap, intersect-empty fail-closed, outage fallback), **schema drift guard** for migration 0050 constraints, updated `upload.controller.spec` (effective-policy presign, verified detected-type flow, spoofed-content-type rejection).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Admin configures upload policies (allowed formats + size limits) per category (documents, images, videos) — canonical set `document`/`image`/`video`, versioned rows with effective windows, list/create/end API.
- [x] Within deployment-safe boundaries — write-time validation bounds extensions to the deployment-permitted set and size to the deployment per-category cap (≤ 100 MB); upload path independently enforces `min(DB, deployment)` (resolver tests + service boundary tests).
- [x] Config versioned — effective windows + soft-close (never hard-delete), at most one open policy per category (DB EXCLUDE + service window logic + tests).
- [x] Validate both extension and detected content type at upload — extension/MIME/size at presign against effective policy; magic-byte detection at verify returns `confirmed`/`type_mismatch` (spoofed-content-type test: .pdf-extension PNG rejected).
- [x] System enforces both DB config and deployment-level limits — resolver intersection + min-cap semantics; deployment baseline fallback on missing DB policy or DB outage.
- [x] Audit: `change_recorded` with actor/ip/correlation id on every write; step-up on mutations; permission gate (admin:uploads:edit).
- [x] Migration 0050 backward-compatible (new table only), idempotent, schema drift guard test added.

Admin gift-code management API slice under `api/admin/promotions/gift-codes` (permission `admin:promotions:edit`, step-up on mutations, `change_recorded` audit with correlation id), plus the order-creation redemption seam:

- **Migration 0048** — `gift_codes` (normalized UNIQUE code, fixed_irr / percentage-bps discount with REQUIRED cap for %, eligibility public|profile, total/per-profile limits, date window, min order, eligible categories, status), `gift_code_profiles` (profile-restricted scopes, CASCADE), `gift_code_redemptions` (ledger; UNIQUE `order_id` = one code per order; `consumed`/`released` status). Discount/window/limit CHECKs mirror the service validation; hand-written SQL per repo convention (no journal entry).
- **Shared contract** `@barghsa/shared/promotions` — `normalizeGiftCode` (trim + uppercase), `validateGiftCodePayload`, `computeGiftDiscount` (exact bigint IRR: fixed = min(value, order); % = min(floor(order×bps/10000), cap)). The invoice seam applies VAT **after** this discount on taxable lines.
- **Service** — list (search/status/discountType filters + usage aggregates), stats (per-profile breakdown + recent redemptions), create, update (re-normalized code, unique-excluding-self, profile scopes replaced), active/inactive toggle (same-status no-op), `redeem` (gift_codes row locked `FOR UPDATE`; validates status, window, eligibility, total + per-profile limits, min order, category), `releaseByOrder` (cancel-before-payment restores slots — the default policy).
- **Orders integration** — `createOrder` now runs in ONE transaction and, when an optional `giftCode` is supplied, redeems on the same client: the order insert and redemption commit/roll back together, so failed orders never consume a slot. Order snapshots `gift_code_id` + `gift_discount_amount` (nullable mirror; authoritative link is `gift_code_redemptions.order_id`). New `POST /api/orders/:id/cancel` (DRAFT/PENDING → CANCELLED) releases the slot (idempotent).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Code value case-insensitive unique — normalized (trim+uppercase) on every write/lookup; UNIQUE index in migration; 409 on collision.
- [x] Discount type fixed IRR or percentage with max cap — percentage REQUIRED cap (`maxCapIrr`), fixed forbids cap; enforced in shared validation, zod schema, service, and DB CHECKs.
- [x] Eligibility public / profile-restricted — `gift_code_profiles` scopes; profile mode requires ≥1 profile, enforced at redeem (403 when not eligible).
- [x] Usage limits total + per-profile — null = unlimited; checked under `FOR UPDATE` at redeem; released redemptions stop counting.
- [x] Dates, minimum order amount, eligible categories, status — all validated at redeem; admin toggle with same-status no-op.
- [x] Redemption atomically at order creation — same transaction as the order insert; failed creation rolls back (tested).
- [x] Failed orders don't consume — rollback path tested.
- [x] Cancellation before payment restores by default — `releaseByOrder` flips consumed → released; wired into `POST /api/orders/:id/cancel`.
- [x] VAT calculated after gift discount on taxable lines — `computeGiftDiscount` is the single seam; invoice integration (not yet built) uses it; documented in shared contract.
- [ ] Admin web UI slice (list/search/filter, create/edit form, usage stats, toggle, high-value % warning, fa/en dicts, RTL/a11y) — deferred, matching the S-09 admin API-slice pattern used by T-09.12.01/02.

title: feat(admin): VAT configuration — versioned rates, product overrides, resolution seam (T-09.12.02)

Implements `02-auth-users-admin.md#T-09.12.02`.

## What

Admin VAT configuration API — versioned rates by charge category with optional per-product overrides, effective dating, and the point-in-time resolution seam for invoice-time snapshotting (T-03.02.05.03 consumer).

- **DB (migration 0047)**: `vat_configurations` (category, rate in basis points CHECK 0..10000 = 0%..100%, effective_from/effective_until with GIST no-overlap per category) and `product_vat_overrides` (product_id + vat_config_id FKs, own effective window, GIST no-overlap per product). `updated_at` triggers; schema drift-guard test pins the constraints.
- **Shared (`@barghsa/shared/finance`)**: `CHARGE_CATEGORIES`, basis-point validation (0 ≤ rate ≤ 100%), resolution rules (`resolveVatRate`: product override wins → category default → 0% fallback), window-status derivation (current/scheduled/expired). Unit-tested.
- **Service (`VatConfigService`)**: versioned `createRate` (closes previously-open rate at the new effective_from; same-rate re-submit is a no-op), soft `endRate` (never hard-delete), product override create/end with the same window discipline, and `resolve()` at a point in time. All mutations run in one transaction and write a `change_recorded` audit event with actor/ip/summary.
- **Controller** (`/api/admin/finance/vat`): `GET ?category=`, `POST` (create rate), `POST :id/end`, `GET overrides`, `POST overrides`, `POST overrides/:id/end`, `GET resolve?productId=&category=&at=`. Permission `admin:finance:edit` (mapped to platform admin today, per S-09 convention); step-up required on all mutations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Admin configures VAT rates by charge category — `POST /api/admin/finance/vat` with `category` validated against `CHARGE_CATEGORIES`, rate as basis points.
- [x] Optional product override — `POST /api/admin/finance/vat/overrides` links a product to a rate row with its own effective window.
- [x] Effective dates / versioned — every rate row carries `effective_from`/`effective_until`; new rates append versions and close the previous open one; future-dated rates are allowed.
- [x] Product override wins; category default otherwise; 0% fallback — `resolveVatRate` + service `resolve()` enforce exactly this order.
- [x] Snapshot on invoice at calculation time — `resolve({productId, category, at})` is the seam; invoice calc (T-03.02.05.03) consumes it.
- [x] Rate stored as basis points — integer `rate` column, 900 = 9.00%.
- [x] Audit `change_recorded` — single-tx audit event on every mutation; no-op re-submits write nothing.
- [x] Validation 0 ≤ rate ≤ 100% — zod schema (0..10000), service guard, and DB CHECK triple-enforced.

- **Migration 0041** — `background_jobs` table with CHECK constraints (`failed|retrying|dead_letter|resolved`, `transient|permanent|provider`), a composite list index (`status, first_failed_at DESC`), and a **partial unique index** guaranteeing at most one *active* failure row per job type.

Wired into the outbox poll, service breach scan, and service escalation scan loops in `main.ts`.

title: feat(admin,db,worker,shared): service escalation policy and scanner (T-09.08.03)
body:
Implements `02-auth-users-admin.md#T-09.08.03`.

## What

Escalation alerts sit on top of the T-09.08.01 service breach scan. When an open service item breaches its response target, the breach scanner alerts the **assigned** staff — the level-1 tier. This PR adds the two deeper escalation tiers and the admin policy that drives them:

- **shared/admin `escalation-policy.ts`** — the `admin.escalation_policy` config contract: per service type, a `level2` (team lead) and `level3` (admin) config, each with a `delayHours` (1..8760, `null` disables the tier) and a channel set (`in_app` mandatory, `email` optional). Strict validation, corruption-tolerant normalization, all-disabled defaults (escalation is opt-in). Also registers the `admin.service_escalated` notification event (immediate, system).
- **db migration 0039** — additive `escalation_level` (default 1, terminal 3) and `escalated_at` columns on `service_breach_alerts`, with a `CHECK (escalation_level BETWEEN 1 AND 3)`. `IF NOT EXISTS` / re-appliable. Drift test pins the columns + constraint.
- **API** — `GET`/`PUT /api/admin/config/escalation-policy` behind the S-09.08 `admin:service-escalation:edit` gate (isAdmin today); versioned `app_config` upsert, config-version bump, `config_change` audit with previous value + both versions.
- **Worker `escalation-scanner`** — wired into `main.ts` (default 5m). Advances un-responded episodes level 1 → 2 (team lead) then 2 → 3 (admin). At-most-once per tier via an atomic conditional `UPDATE … WHERE escalation_level = expected`. Source re-verify (open status + per-episode `target_hours` cutoff) so resolved/recovered items are never escalated. No-recipient claims are reverted. Team lead = the responsible user's team members (falls back to admins when the user is in no team, or the item is unassigned); level 3 = admins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Breached target escalates to team lead after `level2.delayHours` of no response (in-app + optional email).
- [x] Escalates to admin after `level3.delayHours` past the level-2 escalation.
- [x] Configurable alert channels (in-app, email) per level.
- [x] Worker loop triggers escalation; at-most-once per tier; no escalation of resolved items.
- [x] Admin API for the escalation policy (versioned, audited `config_change`).

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/shared test` — pass (236, incl. 20 new)
- `pnpm --filter @barghsa/db test` — pass (106, incl. 2 new)

- Migration 0039 + escalation SQL validated on postgres:16 (team-lead resolution, level-2/3 due queries, CHECK constraint)

## Notes

- Team-lead recipient interpretation: the forked staff-team model (T-09.08.02) has no dedicated "lead" role yet, so level 2 escalates to the responsible user's team members; fallback to platform admins when the user belongs to no team or the item is unassigned. A future slice can introduce an explicit team-lead field.

Implements `02-auth-users-admin.md#T-09.07.02` (prerequisite slice of the L-sized dual-approval workflow).

## What

The approval-request domain that the future finance module routes financial actions into when they exceed the configured threshold (T-09.07.01). This slice is scoped to the backend lifecycle so the finance module, step-up flow, and alert pipeline can consume it later without a rewrite:

- **Shared contract** (`@barghsa/shared/finance/approval-request.ts`): action types (`refund`, `manual_adjustment`, `bank_payment_confirmation`), status machine (`pending | approved | rejected`), strict input validation (no coercion — mirroring the threshold validator), and `shouldRequireDualApproval(config, amount)` — the T-09.07.02 routing rule (`thresholdIrR > 0 && amount > threshold`), fully unit-tested.

Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.06.07`.

- New `POST /api/webhooks/email/resend` endpoint (`EmailWebhookModule`) receiving Resend `email.delivered` / `email.bounced` / `email.complained` / `email.opened` / `email.clicked` events.

- **Suppression**: hard bounce and complaint create `email_suppressions` rows (UNIQUE per address+reason), the durable gate future non-essential email sends must check. Complaint recorded as corrective-action record.
- **Config**: new optional `webhook_secret` field on the Resend provider config, encrypted at rest + masked like `api_key` (T-05.06.05 boundary honoured).

title: feat(notifications): email provider circuit breaker (T-05.06.06)
body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.06.06`.

## What
- **`EmailCircuitBreakerService`** (new, provider-config module): persisted, per-provider circuit breaker for the email send path. Tracks consecutive transient failures in a rolling 5-minute window; when the 5th failure lands the provider row is marked `degraded` (new migration 0033 columns on `email_provider_configs`), the send path refuses test-sends, and an ops log/alert is emitted.
- **Half-open recovery**: after a 60s cooldown the breaker allows exactly one probe — a test-send (`testConnection`) — a success resets it to healthy, a failed probe keeps it open and restarts the cooldown (probes spaced by the cooldown, no immediate re-probing).
- **Integration**: `EmailProviderConfigService.testConnection` feeds every outcome into the breaker and throws `409 CONFLICT_STATE` with the cooldown timestamp while the breaker is open; results now expose `degraded`, `degradedReason`, `breakerOpenedAt`, `breakerCooldownUntil`. A `breakerDecision()` gate is exported for the future transport adapter (the SMTP/Resend send transports are wired in a later task; today the worker registers only `in_app`).
- **Metric**: worker `/metrics` now publishes `provider_email_health{provider_id}` (1=healthy, 0=tripped), derived from the same persisted `degraded` flag — single source of truth across API and worker.
- Drizzle schema (`email-provider-configs.ts`) kept in sync with migration 0033.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Track consecutive failures per provider (persisted window on `email_provider_configs`)
- [x] Threshold: 5 consecutive transient failures in 5 minutes trips the breaker (mitigated: window with 60s/5min defaults, unit-tested)
- [x] When tripped: provider marked Degraded + send path stops sending through it (`breakerDecision` gate + test-connection 409) + ops log/alert
- [x] Recovery: 60s cooldown → one test-send probe; success resets breaker, failure keeps it open
- [x] Health metric `provider_email_health{provider_id}` 1=healthy 0=tripped
- [x] Persisted state survives restarts and is shared across worker/API replicas

title: feat(api): provider secrets encryption & masking (T-05.06.05)
body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.06.05`.

## What
Field-level secrets encryption for email provider configs, plus masked API exposure:
- **`ProviderSecretsService`** — AES-256-GCM field-level encryption at rest, `v1:iv:tag:data` envelope, random 96-bit IV per value, fail-closed on tamper or missing key, backward-compatible pass-through of legacy plaintext.
- Encrypt SMTP `password` and Resend `api_key` on **create** and on **update** (the patch is encrypted before the JSONB merge, so omitted secrets are preserved and new ones stop plaintext).
- Decrypt **only at the send boundary** — the SMTP/Resend connection testers and rollback (`readConfig`), never in API results.
- API rows now expose a **`maskedConfig`** view (secret fields shown as `*…last4`) and never return raw/encrypted secrets.
- `PROVIDER_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env var (64-hex → AES-256), documented in `.env.example`; warning logged when unset.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Encrypt at field level before storing in DB (create + update)
- [x] Decrypt only in the send boundary (connection testers / rollback), not in API results
- [x] Mask in API responses: last 4 chars only, rest `*` (`maskedConfig`)
- [x] Secrets never returned to frontend plaintext
- [x] Never logged in plaintext (errors redact via existing sanitizers)
- [x] Tests for transparency + tamper-resistance + secret preservation on edit

## Review round 1 fixes (GLM-5.2 request_changes → addressed)
- **critical** masked-placeholder corruption on update: `encryptConfig` now detects/omits masked display values (`*…last4`) so the JSONB merge preserves the stored secret; added `isMaskedValue` guard + tests.
- **major** admin page crash when key missing & encrypted rows exist: `maskConfig` degrades gracefully → `[encrypted]` instead of throwing.
- **major** no-key contradiction: `encryptConfig` now stores plaintext (documented degradation) when `PROVIDER_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset, matching `.env.example`.
- **major** missing update() encryption coverage: added service tests for password rotation on update, secret preservation on later edits, and masked-placeholder echo.
- **minor** `v1:` prefix collision with a real legacy `v1:...` secret — accepted as follow-up (unlikely; `.env.example` now only issues warning).

body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.06.02` — SMTP configuration.

## What
- New Zod `SmtpConfigSchema` with documented fields & defaults: `host`, `port` (default 587), `security` (`TLS`|`STARTTLS`, default `STARTTLS`), `username`, `password` (encrypted at rest elsewhere — T-05.06.05), `connection_timeout` (default 10s), `command_timeout` (default 15s), `from_name`, `from_email`, `reply_to`.
- New `SmtpConnectionTesterService`: runs a real SMTP handshake (`CONNECT → EHLO → AUTH`) via `nodemailer.transport.verify()` mapped from the parsed config; returns a safe, credential-redacted success/error.
- New `SmtpNetworkGuard` (SSRF defence): blocks loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local, ULA, multicast, documentation, and IPv4-mapped destinations; a deployment-level `SMTP_HOST_ALLOWLIST` env var exempts explicit hosts. Guards before any socket is opened.
- New admin endpoint `POST /api/admin/email-providers/:id/test-connection` that runs the live test and persists the outcome as `last_test_status`/`last_test_error`, returning the updated config + `{ test: { ok, error } }`.
- Added `nodemailer` + `@types/nodemailer` to the API package.

## Acceptance criteria

title: feat(worker): channel availability rules (T-05.05.02)
body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.05.02`.

## What
Channel availability rules for the outbox worker — the consent + verified-destination gate between the lease loop and the transport layer:

- `apps/worker/src/notifications/channel-availability.ts` — pure decision module. For **mandatory/system** events the `in_app` channel always delivers; an external leg (`email`/`sms`) sends only when the recipient profile owns a **verified destination** for it. For **marketing** events, external legs send only when the profile has **opted in** to that channel *and* owns a verified destination. `in_app` is never consent-gated. Unknown event keys default to mandatory (safe).
- `apps/worker/src/notifications/channel-availability-loader.ts` — resolves a row's verified contacts (`users.email` / `users.mobile`) and per-channel marketing consent (`user_notification_preferences`) from the DB; returns a conservative empty context (skip external) when the recipient is missing.
- `apps/worker/src/notifications/outbox-runner.ts` — applies the gate to each leased row before dispatch, dispatching only the allowed channels and recording a skipped external leg as a terminal `failed` job with a `permanent skipped:<reason>` delivery-log row (never dead-lettered, never retried, never blocks the in-app/allowed legs).
- Unit tests (gate matrix) + loader tests + an integration test in `outbox-runner.test.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] **Transactional notifications always delivered (in-app)** — mandatory/system rows always keep `in_app`; external follow verified destinations.
- [x] **Marketing requires opt-in, separate from transactional** — marketing external legs skipped with reason when not opted-in; mandatory never requires consent.
- [x] **Security-critical not disabled** — mandatory (incl. security-pinned OTP/auth) in-app leg can never be dropped by the gate.

title: feat(e05): dead-letter queue & admin UI (T-05.01.06)
body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.01.06`.

## What
Dead-letter queue for notification deliveries that exhaust their retry budget, with an admin triage panel.

- **DB:** `notification_dead_letter` table (migration 0027, journal idx 27 registered) + Drizzle schema + package exports. Inherits failed delivery context (outbox/job ids, channel, event key, severity, sanitized cause, error category, attempts, idempotency key, status). `job_id` is UNIQUE (idempotent/re-open key). Indexes for ops-panel query shapes (open-first, severity, per-outbox).
- **Worker:** `writeDeadLetter` writer — sanitizes cause, derives severity (`critical` for urgent/security event types via retry-schedule registry, else `error`), classifies the error, and upserts on `job_id`: a job that dead-letters again after an admin Retry re-opens the row with fresh attempt data instead of silently disappearing (`ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE`). Wired into `outbox-runner.persistOutcomes` and the `failAllJobs` exception path whenever a job transitions to `dead_letter`, committed atomically with the job status update on a pinned PG client (fallback to direct queries under the test-only fake pool).
- **Admin API:** `GET /api/admin/notifications/dead-letters` (filter status/severity/channel, open→critical→newest ordering, limit/offset) and `POST .../:id/{retry|resolve|dismiss}`. Retry re-queues the job and parent outbox (both `attempts` reset to 0) with the same idempotency key (at-most-once preserved from T-05.01.04), in one `pool.connect()` transaction; Resolve/Dismiss mark terminal. Idempotent after first action; returns the full updated row.
- **Admin UI:** `DeadLetterPanel` mounted in AdminNotificationsPage — severity/cause/attempts/date, open/all toggle, and Retry/Resolve/Dismiss actions, with fa/en i18n for all labels and access-denied/action-error handling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Dead-letter table inherits failed delivery data
- [x] Admin panel shows dead-letter deliveries with severity, cause, attempt history (attempts/max + delivery-log via existing endpoint)
- [x] Retry re-queues with the same idempotency key
- [x] Resolve marks final, no retry

title: feat(e05): durable outbox write pipeline — transactional enqueue + dispatch runner (T-05.01.02)
body:
Implements `05-notifications-documents-ai.md#T-05.01.02`.

## What
- **Transactional enqueue** (`apps/worker/src/notifications/outbox-writer.ts`): `enqueueOutbox()` writes a `notification_outbox` row plus one `notification_job` per channel atomically inside the caller's already-open PG transaction (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the unique idempotency key and on `(outbox_id, channel)`), guaranteeing delivery intent is durable in the same commit as the business event and at-most-once semantics on re-fire. Default idempotency key = `sha256(eventKey:profileId)`.
- **Dispatch runner** (`outbox-runner.ts`): `runOutboxPoll()` leases due rows (`leaseOutbox`), marks them `sending`, dispatches every requested channel (`dispatchOutbox`), then records `delivered` / `failed` on both the outbox row and its jobs, incrementing attempts and stashing a safe `last_error`.
- **Worker wiring** (`main.ts`): replaced the placeholder loop with an outbox poll loop (2s default, `OUTBOX_POLL_MS`), drain-aware and stopped on SIGTERM/SIGINT.
- Added `pg` + `@types/pg` to the worker for `PoolClient` typing; unit tests for the writer (6) and runner (4).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `notification_outbox` durable table designed (from T-05.01.01) with idempotency key, lease, attempts, scheduled_for — reused; no schema change needed.
- [x] Write outbox rows in the same PG transaction as the business event (`enqueueOutbox` issues INSERTs against the caller-owned transaction; never commits independently).
- [x] Outbox reader worker picks unlocked rows, claims lease, dispatches (`leaseOutbox` → `runOutboxPoll` → `dispatchOutbox` status bookkeeping).
- [ ] Live end-to-end dispatch against a running DB — integration/e2e level (not run in this tick).

body:
Implements `04-invoices-wallet-contracts.md#T-04.1.01.01`.

## What
- Create `packages/db/src/schema/invoices.ts` — the `invoices` table defining the full invoice lifecycle structure:
  - `id` (UUIDv7), `profileId` (FK → profiles), optional `orderId` (FK → orders, set-null), optional `contractId` (text; contracts table TBD)

- Add `export * from './schema/invoices'` to the `packages/db` barrel file

- [x] State column reflects the 9-state invoice state machine

title: feat(packages/db): implement query timeout and cancellation (T-02.01.03)
body:
Implements `01-platform-infrastructure.md#T-02.01.03`.

## What
- Add `queryTimeout` option to `DbPoolConfig` (default `30_000` ms), matching the default `statement_timeout` GUC so client-side cancellation can complement the server-side guard.
- Rename `attachSlowQueryLogging` → `attachClientQueryHooks`; it now enforces a client-side query timeout in any environment.
- When a query exceeds `queryTimeout`, emit a structured `query_timeout` warning and send a PostgreSQL cancel request via the client's cancel protocol (`client.cancel()`).

- Add tests covering `queryTimeout` config acceptance and the 30s default.

title: feat: implement bundle budget checking in CI (T-01.03.04)
body:
Implements `01-platform-infrastructure.md#T-01.03.04`.

## What
- Install `size-limit` and `@size-limit/preset-app` as root devDependencies
- Create `.size-limit.json` with per-route JS gzip budgets as specified in the task
- Add `check:bundle` script to root `package.json`
- Add `check:bundle` step to CI workflow after integrity checks

## Per-route budget tracking
The task specifies: login/register ≤150KB, dashboard ≤300KB, electricity ordering ≤250KB, admin ≤500KB.

Currently login/register/dashboard/electricity ordering all share one Vite entry chunk (`index-*.js`), so individual per-route measurement is not possible until those routes get their own chunks via lazy-loading. The combined budget of **700 KB gzip** (sum of 150+300+250) serves as the guardrail until route-level splitting is implemented. Admin (500 KB) is independently tracked because admin routes are already lazy-loaded.

When a future task introduces route-level splitting for dashboard/electricity routes, this config should be split into separate entries per route.

## Acceptance criteria
